#4404. Here's Every New Electric Vehicle Model for Sale in the U.S. for 2027

Range, efficiency, and base price: This guide will help you decide on the EV that works best for you.

Electric vehicles make up a small percentage of the total automotive market today, but their appeal continues to grow as the automakers expand their range, performance, and style—and as recharging becomes quicker and easier. Shoppers looking for zero-emissions driving now have an expansive list of vehicles to choose from, with a wide variety of body styles and several different price points. To make it easy on you, we've compiled them all in one place so you can choose the best EV that's right for your family, lifestyle, and driving habits. Please note that this list includes only those EVs that draw their power from the country's electrical power grid, which means it doesn’t include the few available fuel-cell cars that propel themselves with electricity but are fueled by hydrogen.

Think of the A6 e-tron as the electric equivalent to Audi's long-running gas-powered A6 sedan, pairing handsome, if reserved, styling with impressive range. There's also a sportier S6 e-tron variant that produces nearly 500 horsepower.

The e-tron GT is effectively a Porsche Taycan in Audi clothing. It's a quick and fun sports sedan that's neither particularly spacious nor inexpensive.

The Q4 e-tron is Audi's compact electric SUV, and shares components with the Volkswagen ID.4. The Q4 e-tron is offered as both a traditional SUV and as a Sportback model with a more coupe-like roofline.

The Audi Q6 e-tron is a compact electric luxury SUV that is around seven inches longer than the Q4 e-tron. Audi also offers the performance-focused SQ6 e-tron, which features a more potent dual-motor powertrain. Both the Q6 and SQ6 are offered as a Sportback variant with a sloping roofline.

BMW's electric equivalent to the gas- and gas-electric 5-series goes by the name i5, and it's arguably the better-driving mid-size BMW sedan option.

The i7 is the electric sister vehicle to BMW’s long-running flagship sedan, the 7-series, and shares its bold design with its gas-powered relative.

The BMW iX3 is a compact luxury SUV that is essentially the electric equivalent of the brand’s popular X3 gas-powered SUV. It is the first BMW EV to reach the U.S. riding on the company’s Neue Klasse platform.

The Cadillac Optiq is a compact electric luxury SUV that utilizes the same platform and powertrain as the Chevrolet Equinox EV, and is also offered with a performance-oriented V-series model.

Cadillac’s first entry into the luxury electric SUV category is the slick-looking Lyriq. It shares its battery tech with other high-profile GM EVs, including the GMC Hummer EV pickup truck, but it wears a more upscale wardrobe. The rear-wheel-drive model offers the most range. The all-wheel-drive model adds an additional electric motor to produce a combined 500 horsepower. Unlike Caddy’s sports sedans, the Lyriq’s driving demeanor takes on a more comfortable, cruising-focused feel, and the quiet cabin is spacious for both people and cargo.

The Cadillac Vistiq is a mid-size electric luxury SUV with three rows of seating, which slots in above the Lyriq and serves as an effective replacement for the gas-powered XT6.

The Cadillac Escalade IQ is a full-size luxury SUV that borrows the first part of its name from Cadillac's long-running gas-powered behemoth but features an electric powertrain under its bold bodywork. Cadillac also offers an IQL variant that is 4.2 inches longer, providing extra third-row legroom and cargo space.

The Celestiq is an ultra-luxurious behemoth, measuring over 18 feet long and packed with modern tech and rich materials. Each Celestiq is special-ordered, entirely bespoke, and incredibly expensive, with prices starting around $340,000.

The Bolt returns after a brief hiatus as Chevy's smallest and most affordable EV, starting at just $28,995.

The Chevrolet Equinox EV is a compact electric SUV that carries a starting price of just under $35,000.

Apart from being a midsize two-row Chevy SUV wearing aggressive styling, the Blazer EV shares little in common with its gas-powered relative. The Blazer EV comes in three trim levels: LT, RS, and SS. Many drivetrain combinations are available, ranging from a mild single-motor front-wheel-drive setup for the base LT to a wild 550-plus horsepower dual-motor all-wheel-drive fitment for the SS. Additionally, there are two lithium-ion battery packs to choose from. Range varies depending on battery and motor configuration.

Despite sharing its name with the conventionally powered Silverado truck, the Silverado EV is a clean-sheet design and is offered in a wide range of configurations, from a work truck to the high-powered 760-hp LT and the off-road-tuned Trail Boss.

The Dodge Charger Daytona is an electric muscle car and Dodge's first electric vehicle, available as both a two-door coupe and a four-door sedan.

The Fiat 500 hatchback returns to our shores for 2024. Except this time, it's an electric-only affair, as reflected by its 500e moniker. Though this little Fiat oozes style, its driving range is a bit disappointing. Though the EPA has yet to release an official estimate, Fiat is advertising an estimated 149-mile range from this sub-$40,000 city car.

Although legally considered a "Low Speed Vehicle," the Topolino can be converted to be road legal and provides a new entry point for the EV market with its $14,985 price tag. Just don't expect it to do all the same things a normal car can do, with a top speed of just 25 mph and a range of 46 miles.

It may not have two doors or a V-8, but the Ford Mustang Mach-E has the looks and driving dynamics to warrant its wearing of the Blue Oval's pony car nameplate.

#4403. The AI Boom Is Creating A New Supply Chain Headache For Automakers

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

The auto industry may be headed for another chip crunch. Last time, it was the pandemic that snarled supply chains and threw the chip market out of whack. This time, the AI boom is squeezing the supply of the basic semiconductors that modern cars rely on.

The CEO of Dutch semiconductor manufacturer Nexperia, Stefan Tilger, told Reuters that competitors had shifted supply for commodity semiconductors toward chips used in AI data center. And since a great deal of that production was once dedicated to mature chips (like those used in cars and other industrial equipment), a bottleneck is quickly brewing in the automotive supply chain. The auto industry is "suffering quite heavily," he said.

STMicroelectronics, a Swiss semiconductor manufacturer, is seeing the same problem, according to comments reported by the outlet. CEO Jean-Marc Chery warns that chip foundries and assembly plants are increasingly "disengaging" from traditional mainstream automotive and industrial applications. Tilger says that another emerging area eating into the supply chain is the new breed of robotics beginning to hit the market.

Both company leaders are stressing that the upcoming shortage isn't because big GPU companies like Nvidia are eating up every last chip known to man. The squeeze is happening even further upstream in the supply chain.

And the auto industry is already feeling the impact. German automotive supplier Aumovio, which makes sensors, cameras, and other in-vehicle electronics for customers like BYD, BMW, and Ford, warned on a recent earnings call that its chip costs are rising and will "explode" next year.

"What is the reason for that situation? The reason are the data centers for mainly artificial intelligence," said interim finance head Claus Bauer. "We can tell you that there's no price sensitivity whatsoever in that area. All of our suppliers in that regard could sell twice their capacity to this very lucrative, non-price-sensitive area."

Automakers are no strangers to semiconductor shortages. During the pandemic, chip shortages forced car companies to idle production lines and even ship cars without certain computer-reliant features, like automatic start/stop. It's not clear yet that things will get as bad as last time. But if they do, the AI-driven race to make everything smarter could lead to less-smart cars, if only temporarily.

#4402. Watch BYD’s robotic charging arm plug itself in and charge EVs in 5 minutes [Video]

BYD’s Flash Charging tech can charge an EV in as little as five minutes. Now, BYD is taking things a step further with integrated solar power and a robotic arm that plugs itself in. See how it all works in action.

After unveiling the Yangwang Altior in the UAE on Monday, its new ultra-luxury flagship electric sedan, BYD showcased its latest breakthrough technology.

The Chinese automaker launched a new integrated charging system in the Abu Dhabi desert that brings BYD’s “Three Green Dreams” to life.

In 2006, BYD president and CEO Wang Chuanfu revealed his vision of “Three Green Dreams,” including harnessing solar power to generate renewable energy, storing that energy in batteries, and replacing gas-powered vehicles with electric ones that run on clean energy.

The new charging system is the “world’s first,” according to BYD, to integrate solar power generation, energy storage, Flash Charging, and robotic charging together in one solution.

BYD’s Flash Charging tech enables a vehicle’s battery to charge from 10% to 70% in five minutes, essentially the same time it takes to fill up at a gas station. For a full recharge, or to go from 10% to 97%, it takes just nine minutes.

The new robotic charging arm automatically locates the vehicle’s charging port, opens its cover, plugs in, and then removes it once the session is over.

By combining robotic charging with its Automated Valet Parking, BYD said the new tech goes beyond automated driving and parking to the charging process itself.

Once the vehicle is parked, the robotic charging arm automatically takes over and connects it to Flash Charging without the driver even touching the cable.

A post shared by Michael Martinez (@mmichael_martinez)

Michaël Martinez, head of marketing at BYD France, posted a video (shown above) showcasing the new charging tech in action.

The integrated solution is built around BYD’s Solar-Storage-Charging (SSC) system, fusing solar energy generation, battery storage, and its 5-minute Flash Charging tech. Together, the setup captures energy from the sun, stores it, and distributes it as needed.

If they could tie this into a smart summon type of capability, where the vehicle communicates with the charger and moves the vehicle into the proper location for charging and then moves to a parking spot once charging is complete. Rental car fleets would benefit and so would those in shopping centers. There are so many possibilities and this looks far more mature that the old snake charging Tesla demoed.

BYD has over 16 years of experience in the solar industry with a portfolio that includes solar cells, modules, and systems.

Its solar division, BYD Solar, does business in over 100 countries and regions. By using solar power, BYD said, the SCC system can operate independently off-the-grid.

The new technology is part of BYD’s wider Flash Charging rollout. By the end of 2027, the company plans to deploy 6,000 Flash Charging stations globally.

#4401. Every EV from Every Brand in America

We've created this handy guide to let you know all the brands that sell electric vehicles in the United States.

While gas-powered vehicles still make up an overwhelming majority of cars sold in the United States, their market share is slowly getting chipped away at by battery-electric ones. Since the Nissan Leaf and Tesla Roadster brought electric vehicles back to the national stage in the late 2000s, automakers have worked overtime to noticeably improve the charging speeds and driving ranges of their battery-powered products. No longer limited to small cars, EVs now take up space in just about every automotive segment.

We've compiled an exhaustive list of today's options to make it easy to determine what electric vehicles are available from which automotive brands in the United States. Don't go looking for hydrogen-powered electric vehicles here, though, as we've excluded those from this list.

Audi sells an array of electric SUVs and cars, from the compact Q4 e-tron to the range-topping 912-hp RS e-tron GT. Both of Audi's electric SUVs are available in either wagon or fastback body styles.

BMW's EV sedans look similar to their gas-powered cars, but the iX3 and incoming i3 promise next-generation looks and technology.

Cadillac's lineup of electric vehicles consists of an SUV in nearly every size, including the Escalade IQ, which looks just as ostentatious as the gas-powered Escalade despite its silent powertrain.

Chevrolet's electric vehicle arsenal is centered around SUVs, but the American automaker also caters to business owners with the WT version of the Silverado EV pickup truck.

Dodge currently sells just one EV, the Charger Daytona, which is available as either a coupe or sedan. It assumes the muscle car role vacated by the previous Scat Pack and Hellcat versions of the Charger and Challenger.

The only Fiat sold in the United States right now is an electric version of the company's iconic 500 city car. Fiat also offers the Topolino, which is technically classified as a "Low Speed Vehicle" and is limited to 25 mph.

Ford sells two electric models, the Mustang Mach-E SUV and the E-Transit commercial van.

The Genesis Electrified GV70 is based on the Korean automaker's popular compact SUV, while the GV60 utilizes the same platform found under the Hyundai Ioniq 5 and Kia EV6.

GMC's lineup of electric vehicles is just as big and brash as its gas-powered offerings. Two pickups and an SUV are available.

Hyundai has won Car and Driver's EV of the Year award three times in a row, first with the Ioniq 5 SUV in 2022 and then with the Ioniq 6 sedan in 2023. The high-powered Ioniq 5 N, which entertains with faux gearshifts and engine noises, won the award in 2024.

Jeep currently sells two EVs in the U.S. Although the Wagoneer S shares the first part of its name with the gas-powered Wagoneer, the EV is completely unrelated to that behemoth. The Recon is an electric alternative to the off-road-ready Wrangler.

Kia's lineup of EVs currently consists of a trio of SUVs.

Lexus currently sells two EVs in the United States: the RZ SUV, which is related to the Toyota bZ, and an electric version of the ES sedan.

California-based startup Lucid Motors exclusively builds EVs and recently launched its second model, the Gravity SUV.

The Italian luxury brand currently offers three EVs in the U.S., all of which are related to the brand's gas-powered models and carry the Folgore suffix to distinguish them as battery-powered.

Mercedes offers a vast range of EVs, from sedans to SUVs and even vans. The automaker has begun shifting away from its "EQ" naming structure for EVs, starting with the electric G-class, which dons the name G580 with EQ Technology. It's a wordy solution that'll also appear on the upcoming battery-electric 2026 CLA-class.

While Mini previously sold an electric variation of its iconic Cooper hatchback, the latest version has been delayed indefinitely, meaning Mini currently offers just one EV in the U.S., a battery-powered variant of its Countryman SUV

Nissan sells one EV in the United States, the Leaf, which has transformed from a hatchback to an SUV for its third generation.

There are currently three Porsche EVs on sale in the U.S., with an electric successor to its 718 sports car on the way.

Ram, the truck division spun off from Dodge in 2009, currently sells one EV. Ram had originally aimed to start building the 1500 REV in late 2024 for deliveries in early 2025, but the electric pickup truck is now delayed to late 2026.

#4399. Ori Creator Is Very Unhappy With How Nintendo Handled Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake

Covering the video games industry since 2017, with experience in news, articles, and reviews. Currently a writer at DualShockers and gaming magazines.

We all know that few games have left as lasting an impression on the gaming industry as The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Even decades after its original release, the Nintendo classic continues to inspire developers and entire generations of players.

And its recently released remake has already brought plenty of attention back to Hyrule, with many critics and players praising its beautiful new presentation and sharing emotional reactions to revisiting one of their favorite adventures – no wonder it’s already one of the highest-rated games ever!

However, not everyone is completely satisfied with Nintendo's approach. Thomas Mahler, best known as the creator of the acclaimed Ori franchise, has shared a rather lengthy criticism of the remake on X (formerly Twitter), explaining why he believes the developer missed an opportunity to make the experience much better from a game design perspective.

Mahler recently shared his thoughts on social media after playing the Ocarina of Time remake alongside his son, who was immediately impressed by its new art direction. The developer even mentioned that his son was so amazed by the visuals that he tried touching the screen to grab the Kokiri Sword when he first obtained it, which is pretty cute!

The remake's dev team included younger folks, several of whom never played the original Ocarina of Time, who provided a much-needed modern view of things.

Unfortunately, Mahler himself wasn't nearly as impressed with the experience. In his post, he curiously explained that he has always been somewhat disappointed by the original Ocarina of Time, particularly when comparing it to A Link to the Past. For him, the Nintendo 64 adventure feels emptier and more confusing, and the problem now is that the remake hasn't addressed those issues.

Thomas Mahler, best known as the creator of the acclaimed Ori franchise, has shared a rather lengthy criticism of the remake, explaining why he believes the developer missed an opportunity to make the experience much better from a game design perspective.

His biggest complaint revolves around Hyrule Field, which he considers one of the game's weakest areas. Mahler believes its relatively empty design was understandable back in 1998, considering the Nintendo 64's technical limitations. However, with modern hardware and the technology available today, he feels Nintendo could have done much more than simply improve its appearance. “Sure, Hyrule Field looks prettier now, but it's still just as empty and uninteresting as it was back then,” Mahler explained.

Mahler believes the remake could have taken a similar approach to A Link to the Past by introducing more activities, hidden areas, and interactions throughout Hyrule Field. He also suggested that acquiring new dungeon items should encourage players to revisit previously explored locations and discover paths or secrets they couldn't access before.

Instead, he feels Nintendo preserved an outdated design that could have benefited from a more substantial overhaul. He even argued that the game would deserve a 7.5 or 8 out of 10 today, rather than the perfect scores some reviewers have awarded it.

Eiji Aonuma and the development team for the Ocarina of Time remake discussed how one of the original's infamous dungeons is being improved.

Naturally, Mahler's comments didn't go unnoticed, and plenty of Zelda fans pushed back against his opinion. Some questioned whether changing the original game's structure would undermine what made Ocarina of Time so special in the first place.

The developer wasn't particularly convinced by those arguments, however, and continued defending his position in the replies. “Let's be a bunch of bozos instead who praise 1998 game design and act like it's the end all be all even though Nintendo themselves would never ever design a shit overworld like that for their next mainline entry," he responded.

It's worth noting that Mahler did acknowledge the remake's impressive visuals, and his criticism is primarily directed at its level design rather than its presentation. Still, his comments highlight an interesting discussion about how much developers should change when revisiting beloved classics.

After all, preserving what made a game special and improving the elements that haven't aged quite as well aren't necessarily mutually exclusive. And while plenty of players are clearly enjoying their return to Hyrule, Mahler's reaction shows that even a legendary adventure like Ocarina of Time won't be everyone's cup of tea.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is one of the most beloved games of all time, but these remakes might be just as meaningful to fans.

#4398. Tesla Cybertruck had its best month in over a year. It’s still going away

New EV prices edged up in October, but buyers still paid less than they did a year ago. The average transaction price for a new EV in the US was $56,220, up 1% from September and down 2.7% from October 2025, according to Kelley Blue Book, a Cox Automotive brand.

Across all new vehicles, the average hit a record $51,109, up 1.3% from September and 2.1% year over year, even as prices rose more slowly than they typically do in October.

EV incentives barely budged from September’s revised 11.2% of the average transaction price to 11.3% in October. That’s up from 10.3% a year earlier and well above October’s industrywide average of 6.8%.

Tesla’s average selling price fell from September to $54,194, but it was still up 1.2% year over year. The Cybertruck helped push that average higher. Cox Automotive estimates Tesla sold 1,914 Cybertrucks in October, its best month in more than a year, at an average price of $92,380.

"Tesla sold 1,914 Cybertrucks in October"

About 40 trucks per state? That is way too many. I am not sure if my eyes can handle it.

The strange thing is that I see more Cybertruck around me being driven by Tesla Energy than regular Cybertruck owners.

That sales bump comes as Tesla prepares to end Cybertruck production at its Austin factory in mid-2027. Elon Musk said Tesla will dismantle the assembly line around June or July to make room for more Cybercab robotaxis.

#4397. 2027 VinFast VF8

See all results for new 2027 VinFast VF8 for sale near 31548

VinFast is probably a brand name you’ve not heard before, and that’s because the Vietnam-based company has been selling electric SUVs here for only a few years. The VF8, introduced in 2023, hasn’t sold in significant numbers. In fact, there were no 2026 VF8s, but after skipping a model year, it's back for 2027.

The VF8 is compelling on paper, with a long list of standard amenities and an attractive starting price. All models are all-wheel drive and feature two electric motors generating 349 or 402 horsepower, depending on trim. It's on the road where things quickly fall apart. The VF8’s road manners are rough, its driving range is uncompetitive with similarly priced rival EV SUVs, and its onboard infotainment tech is a nightmare of unintuitive menus and software bugs.

Expert Tip: If an affordable, scienced-out electric SUV with decent range and a long warranty is what you’re after, consider the Hyundai Ioniq 5 or the Kia EV6 instead.

After taking the 2026 model year off, the VF8 is back, sporting a lower starting price. The Eco trim’s $41,790 ask represents a $5410 drop from the 2025 model, and the Plus’s $46,990 price is $6010 less than it was previously. VinFast has improved the VF8’s driver-assistance offerings this year too, adding rear automated emergency braking, an intersection assist system, an automatic lane-changing feature, evasive steering assist, and a feature that will bring the car to a stop if it detects that the driver has become unresponsive.

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

An all-wheel-drive electric powertrain with two electric motors makes 349 horsepower in the Eco trim and 402 horsepower in the Plus model. While acceleration is respectable for a compact electric SUV, the VF8 falls short in other, subjective areas. For example, the VF8 we sampled was bouncy on uneven roads and its steering required too much effort.

In Comparison: The VF8 Plus’s 60 mph time in our testing is a half second behind the less powerful, 320-hp Hyundai Ioniq 5.

In Comparison: The VF8’s 3,968-pound towing capacity is stout, and although hooking up a trailer of that weight will reduce overall driving range, it is a higher maximum capacity than rivals such as the Ford Mustang Mach-E and the Hyundai Ioniq 5.

As its name suggests, the Eco model can go further on a single charge with an estimated range of 256 miles. The Plus model is rated at 224 miles of range. The VF8’s range figures lag other competitors in the segment. Similarly priced versions of the Tesla Model Y offer ranges stretching as high as 355 miles per charge. When plugged into a DC fast-charger, VinFast claims that the VF8’s battery can charge from 10 to 70 percent in just 31 minutes.

The EPA estimates that the VF8 Eco is good for 77 MPGe city, 69 MPGe highway, and 73 MPGe combined; the Plus model is rated for 75 MPGe city, 71 MPGe highway, and 73 MPGe combined. When we have a chance to take a VF8 on our 75-mph highway fuel economy route, we'll update this story with real-world test results. For more information about the VF8's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.

First Row: The VF8's interior presentation is simple and minimalistic, tossing out traditional driver-facing gauges in favor of a head-up display. Unfortunately, the interior looks more premium than it feels to the touch, and we found the model we drove to be noisy over rough pavement. There are plenty of amenities, though, even in the base Eco trim. Heated front seats, a heated steering wheel, dual-zone automatic climate control, and faux leather upholstery are standard on all trims.

Second Row: Both rows of seats take full advantage of the space available, and the VF8 feels roomy inside. A pair of adults of above-average height will find plenty of legroom and headroom in the back seat. The Plus trim comes with heated outboard rear seats.

Cargo Capacity: The VF8 does offer a commendable amount of storage, though, with both a traditional rear hatch area and a frunk. In our testing, we fit eight carry-on suitcases in the VF8’s cargo bay; with the rear seats folded, we fit a total of 24.

A large 15.6-inch dashboard-mounted display shows vehicle information and doubles as a digital gauge display. For drivers who prefer to have critical information in front of them, a configurable head-up display comes standard and can project information such as speed, state of charge, and navigation onto the windshield. After getting a chance to use the VF8’s infotainment system, we noted that it was laggy and unintuitive compared to that of other vehicles, which will frustrate anyone expecting response speeds and user-friendly navigation of a smartphone.

All VF8 models come with a comprehensive package of driver-assistance features, including conveniences such as automatic high-beam headlamps and traffic sign recognition. In our experience, they worked well, but if you want to turn them off, you'll have to do it each time on startup, which is annoying. Even then, the VF8 will beep and boop with alerts as you approach lane markings or accidentally get too close to another car in traffic.

For information about the VF8’s crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

VinFast offers a generous 10-year/125,000-mile warranty, which should help assuage the fears that come with taking on the risk of buying an electric SUV from an unknown brand. Only Genesis, Kia, and Hyundai come close to VinFast's powertrain warranty with their 10-year policy that extends to 100,000 miles.

#4395. Lucid CEO admits it ‘did not even know where cars were’ and lost orders

Lucid (LCID) CEO Silvio Napoli admitted on the company’s Q3 earnings call that, as recently as this summer, the automaker “did not even know where cars were.” Buyers placed orders, Lucid took up to two weeks to locate and deliver a car, and some of those buyers walked away.

That’s a rough admission from a company sitting on thousands of unsold vehicles. And it’s a problem Tesla ran into, and fixed, back in 2018 at more than ten times Lucid’s current volume.

Napoli made the comment when an analyst asked whether Lucid’s deliveries would go up or down in the fourth quarter. He said that at the start of Q3, the company had orders where it “would take sometimes two weeks to deliver to the customer, and so we would lose the order.”

He said Lucid now has visibility on which cars are being built, where they’re shipped, where they’re stored, and when they can reach a customer. A new commercial team also now sells the cars it knows are available on the day a customer wants one.

Lucid built 3,228 more vehicles than it delivered in the first half of 2026, including 5,500 built but only 3,093 delivered in Q1. Its inventory hit $1.38 billion on the balance sheet at the end of June, which is why we reported earlier this year that Lucid had to adjust production after a bloated Q1 inventory.

So Lucid had thousands of cars on lots and in transit, and it was still losing buyers because it couldn’t match a car to an order fast enough.

In Q3, Lucid cut production to 2,954 vehicles and delivered 3,806, down 7% year over year. Finished goods inventory fell by almost 15% during the quarter, according to new CFO Alexander De Bock. Inventory stood at $1.22 billion on September 30.

Tesla learned this lesson the hard way during the Model 3 ramp.

By Q3 2018, Tesla was making roughly 4,000 Model 3s per week. That’s more cars every week than Lucid delivers in a full quarter today. Deliveries tripled or quadrupled in some markets, and the bottleneck moved from the factory to the trucks.

Elon Musk tweeted in September 2018 that Tesla had “gone from production hell to delivery logistics hell.” A week later, he said Tesla was facing an “extreme shortage of car carrier trailers” and had started building its own car carriers to keep cars moving. Tesla also launched door-to-door delivery and asked existing owners to help at delivery centers.

It didn’t stop there. In November 2018, with the federal tax credit about to be cut in half for Tesla buyers, Musk said Tesla had bought trucking companies and locked in contracts with major haulers. Tesla moved cars east by truck instead of rail to cut weeks off transit times.

Tesla delivered 83,500 vehicles in Q3 2018, including 55,840 Model 3s, a record at the time.

When Model 3 reached Europe in February 2019, the first ship docked at Zeebrugge in Belgium and Tesla immediately had trouble processing the cars at the port.

About a week after the first ship arrived, Tesla ended its contract with the company preparing Model 3s at the port and took over the work itself. The target was 3,000 cars per week coming through one port.

It worked. By March 2019, Tesla delivered more than 5,300 Model 3s in Norway alone, making it the best-selling car in the country by a wide margin. A car that’s sitting at a port or on a lot doesn’t make anyone money. Tesla treated delivery speed as a sales tool, not a back-office job.

We later learned from Musk himself that this “logistic hell” was almost the nail in Tesla’s coffin. The CEO said that Tesla was at the brink of bankruptcy at the time.

This is one of the most embarrassing admissions we’ve heard on an earnings call, and credit to Napoli for saying it out loud. Most executives would have blamed “demand” and moved on.

But it explains a lot. Lucid’s problem has never been the cars. The Air and Gravity are excellent products. The problem has been everything around them: service, software, and now we learn, basic inventory tracking. When you’re spending about $273,000 for every car you deliver, losing a buyer because you can’t find their car two weeks after they ordered is brutal.

Tesla solved this at 4,000 Model 3s a week while fighting for its own survival. Lucid is moving fewer than 300 cars a week. This isn’t a hard problem at that scale. It’s a discipline problem, and Napoli is right to call it that.

#4392. NASA’s Voyager 1 is about to reach a historic one-light-day milestone

Nearly 50 years after leaving Earth, NASA's Voyager 1 is approaching an extraordinary milestone that will highlight just how far humanity's most distant spacecraft has traveled. But keeping the aging explorer operational has become an increasingly difficult challenge as its power supply slowly fades.

NASA engineers recently achieved two important developments in their effort to extend the mission. In September, they completed a complex energy conservation project designed to preserve the spacecraft's remaining scientific capabilities. Then, on October 20, Voyager 1 unexpectedly resumed communication with Earth after a mysterious 48-hour interruption.

NASA Engineers Find a Clever Way to Save Power

In early September, the Voyager team successfully replaced three devices aboard Voyager 1 with alternatives that consume less electricity. The carefully coordinated operation, nicknamed the "Big Bang," took months to prepare and was completed approximately six weeks after engineers carried out an identical procedure on Voyager 2.

The upgrade is expected to extend the operating lives of Voyager 1's remaining scientific instruments, allowing the spacecraft to continue collecting valuable information from interstellar space longer than previously expected.

Both Voyager spacecraft generate electricity using radioisotope thermoelectric generators. These systems produce electrical power from the heat released as plutonium undergoes radioactive decay. As that process continues, the spacecraft gradually lose generating capacity, with each probe experiencing a decline of approximately 4 watts annually.

After almost five decades in space, that steady loss has left engineers with very little power to spare. To keep the missions operating, NASA has progressively shut down equipment that is no longer essential.

The Big Bang presented an especially difficult engineering challenge because all three replacements had to happen simultaneously. The six devices involved help maintain temperatures inside the spacecraft despite the extreme cold of space. Replacing the three original devices together was necessary to reduce electricity consumption while preserving the proper distribution of heat throughout Voyager 1.

Keeping Voyager 1's Science Mission Alive

Power limitations have already forced NASA to deactivate two of Voyager 1's scientific instruments in recent years. When the spacecraft launched in 1977, it carried 10 instruments dedicated to scientific research. Several were shut down after Voyager completed its encounters with the outer planets, while others remained active to investigate increasingly distant regions of space.

Among the areas studied was the outer heliosphere, the enormous region of particles and magnetic fields produced by the Sun. Both Voyager spacecraft have since crossed beyond this boundary into interstellar space, making them the only spacecraft ever to directly examine the environment outside the Sun's heliosphere.

Preserving their remaining instruments is particularly important because no other missions can currently collect measurements from this distant region. Without the Big Bang upgrade, NASA would have faced the possibility of shutting down another Voyager 1 instrument as early as summer 2027.

Mysterious Communication Loss Raises New Questions

Even with the successful power conservation effort, Voyager 1 continues to encounter unexpected problems.

NASA temporarily lost contact with the spacecraft on October 18 and 19, when the agency's Deep Space Network failed to receive its radio signal during two scheduled communication attempts separated by 24 hours.

The network consists of large radio antennas at three locations around the world, allowing NASA to exchange signals with spacecraft exploring the Moon and more distant destinations. At the time of the interruption, Voyager 1 was approximately 16 billion miles (24 billion kilometers) from Earth.

After two unsuccessful attempts to detect the spacecraft, its signal unexpectedly returned on October 20, roughly 48 hours after the interruption began. Communication has remained established since then, and engineers subsequently sent commands to investigate the problem.

NASA has not yet determined exactly what caused the incident. However, engineers discovered that one set of Voyager 1's thrusters had stopped operating and that the spacecraft had automatically activated its backup thrusters.

This behavior is part of a built-in safety system known as fault protection. When the onboard computers recognize a potential problem with active equipment, they can switch to backup hardware, place the spacecraft into a stable configuration, and suspend normal activities. This gives controllers on Earth an opportunity to investigate and determine the appropriate response.

"This is the first time we've seen the spacecraft do something like this, but we are also at a point in the mission where we have to expect the unexpected," said Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California. "We're relieved to be back in contact with Voyager 1 and are eager to understand what happened."

Voyager 1 Approaches a Historic One-Light-Day Milestone

While NASA continues investigating the communication interruption, Voyager 1 is moving toward another remarkable achievement.

Traveling through interstellar space at approximately 38,000 mph (61,155 kph), the spacecraft is expected to reach a distance of 16.09 billion miles (25.89 billion kilometers) from Earth on November 18. That distance equals one light-day, meaning it takes light an entire 24 hours to travel between Earth and the probe.

No other human-made object has ever reached such a distance.

The milestone also illustrates the extraordinary challenges of communicating with a spacecraft so far from home. Radio waves travel at the speed of light, so commands transmitted from Earth will require a full day to reach Voyager 1. Any response sent back will take another 24 hours, creating a total communication delay of 48 hours.

"If you want to say 'hello' to Voyager, you send your message and then you go home and you wait two days before you finally get a response," said Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager at JPL.

Crossing the one-light-day threshold will not produce any physical change in Voyager 1 or its surroundings. The spacecraft will continue traveling through the same interstellar environment, unaware that it has passed a milestone of special significance to people on Earth.

Instead, the achievement serves as a powerful reminder of the enormous distances separating objects in the universe and the remarkable endurance of a spacecraft launched nearly half a century ago. Despite fading power, aging equipment, and unexpected technical problems, Voyager 1 continues its historic journey farther from Earth than any other human-made object.

#4389. Petit Planet’s Gacha System Will Only be For Cosmetics

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

HoYoVerse’s bread and butter is, of course, gacha games. From its first big hit in Honkai Impact 3rd to the breakout success of Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail, and Zenless Zone Zero, gacha is what brings home the bacon. The items distributed through these games’ gacha banners usually include characters, weapons, equipment, and other assorted elements that directly impact your experience with the game. If you want to play, you gotta be willing to roll the dice.

With the looming release of Petit Planet, HoYo’s new Animal Crossing-style life sim game, players have been curious as to how, exactly, the gacha element will factor into this particular style of game. It’d be pretty lousy, for example, if you had to keep rolling on banners just to see all of the game’s villagers and experience their stories.

The new life sim gacha game is launching ahead of several other titles this winter.

However, in a departure from its established formula, HoYo’s actually taking a slightly different approach to monetization in Petit Planet. There will still be a gacha system, of course, but the only items this gacha will dispense will be strictly cosmetic, with all of the actual gameplay stuff being readily accessible to everyone whether they’re willing to roll or not.

At the HoYoverse Media Tour 2026 in Seoul, South Korea, two representatives from the Petit Planet dev team, lead game designer Murphy and lead artist Yinli Huang, explained their philosophy to the surrounding press.

In an interview with gaming outlet Geek Culture, Murphy explained that, rather than paywalling access to the game’s content through gacha banners or direct purchases, the goal is to make all of the actual gameplay elements available to all players, with whatever paid elements there being strictly limited to extra cosmetic stuff like character outfits and furniture.

“All of Petit Planet’s core gameplay, including its life simulation and all content related to forming friendships and building stories with the Neighbours, is included for all free players,” Murphy said. “In terms of our monetisation model, we can confirm that it will only be associated with cosmetics, meaning things like furniture and clothes.”

The goal is to make all of the actual gameplay elements available to all players.

This is quite a departure from HoYo’s other major titles. I play Honkai: Star Rail, for example, and because I don’t have every single character and all of their optimal gacha-earned equipment, I’m basically locked out of the game’s hardest endgame game modes.

Wuthering Waves is one of the biggest Gachas on the planet, and they do far better than most at answering player complaints. Let's go over exactly how!

Petit Planet is slated to specifically be a cozy life sim game rather than a management life sim. Many games of this genre purport to be cozy, but because they demand such constant, consistent engagement from you, they kind of stop being cute little daily life simulators and start being second jobs. The dev team is hoping to use the game’s live-service model to offer consistent, interesting content to the players without directly stoking FOMO.

“As a live-service title, we will constantly add new content to the game, like festival events, which are inspired by real-world festivals, alongside the concept of seasons,” Murphy told Geek Culture. “Each season, players will be able to meet new Neighbours, alongside new clothes and furniture to unlock.”

The crux of this pursuit is an as-of-yet undetermined system that would allow players to properly experience and reap the benefits of seasons’ past even if they weren’t playing the game at the time. Again, Star Rail does regular time-limited events, and while they all offer limited-time currency rewards, the actual gameplay elements remain accessible long after their endpoints. Even so, Murphy wants these types of events in Petit Planet to be as low-pressure as possible so players are interested without feeling obligated.

“We always come back to the randomness in daily life, so there’s no growth curve in our game, we just want to provide more of those little surprises and small pleasures in life for players.”

We were able to get some extensive time with HoYoverse's upcoming life simulator, Petit Planet, and were left grinning from ear-to-ear.

#4388. A clever molecular trick unlocks previously impossible properties in glass

Scientists have developed a new way to change the internal structure of glass while it is being made, giving them greater control over properties such as magnetism and the way the material interacts with light. The discovery could open the door to advanced glasses with capabilities that were previously difficult or impossible to achieve.

The breakthrough comes from a collaboration involving TU Dortmund University, Paderborn University, the University of Duisburg-Essen, and the University of Oxford. Published in Nature Materials, the research demonstrates how adding a particular organic molecule during the melting process can rearrange chemical bonds within certain types of glass.

The method also allows these materials to melt at much lower temperatures, preventing the damage that would otherwise occur during manufacturing. Such specialized glasses have potential applications in gas storage, batteries, optical technologies, and catalysis.

A Molecular Trick That Changes Glass From Within

"We have found a way to chemically modify the structure of glasses derived from so-called metal-organic framework compounds - or MOFs for short - right during the manufacturing process," explains Prof. Dr. Sebastian Henke from TU Dortmund University, who led the study.

The key ingredient is a molecule called 1,10-phenanthroline. When introduced during production, it performs two important tasks. It reduces the temperature needed to melt the material while also changing how metal atoms connect with surrounding molecules.

This combination allows researchers to create glass with magnetic or light-emitting characteristics that previously could not be achieved without exposing the material to potentially destructive temperatures.

To understand why this approach matters, it helps to consider how glass normally forms. When a liquid cools quickly enough, its atoms become locked into a disordered arrangement rather than forming the repeating pattern found in crystals.

"Normally, glass is formed when a molten liquid cools rapidly. The solid structure then sets without the atoms arranging themselves in a regular pattern. Until now, researchers often had to accept the chemistry of these glasses as dictated by the starting material," explains Prof. Henke.

The new findings show that scientists can exert much greater control over this process.

Metal-organic frameworks are materials built from metal centers connected by organic compounds. By introducing phenanthroline while these materials are molten, researchers can change the chemical connections within the structure before the glass solidifies.

"The crucial point is that the molecule does not simply remain as a filler," Prof. Henke continues. "It enters into a reaction. So we are altering the chemistry at precisely the moment when the material is still liquid."

The researchers added phenanthroline to their starting materials before heating them. Once the mixture begins to melt, the molecule does more than simply lower the temperature required for melting. It actively participates in chemical reactions that reorganize the glass network.

The process changes the immediate surroundings of metal atoms by modifying their connections to neighboring molecules.

"As a flux, the substance lowers the temperature at which the material melts; as a chemical agent, the molecule binds directly to the metal atoms and partially displaces old bonds. In the molten state, the molecule interferes with what is known as the coordination environment. This term describes how many neighbors surround a single atom. Because the new molecule binds more strongly to the metal centers, the number of neighbors increases," explains Prof. Henke.

These interactions trigger a substantial rearrangement of the internal glass structure. Importantly, the researchers can control how extensively the material changes simply by adjusting the amount of phenanthroline added.

This gives scientists a practical way to tune the properties of glass during manufacturing rather than relying entirely on the chemistry of the original ingredients.

Lower Temperatures Prevent Damage to Glass

Another major advantage of the discovery is that it overcomes a longstanding problem in manufacturing specialized glasses.

Some of the materials investigated are unable to withstand the temperatures normally required to melt them. Instead of becoming usable glass, they begin to break down, damaging their structure and producing unwanted impurities.

The new molecular approach avoids much of this problem by allowing the materials to melt under gentler conditions.

"Thanks to this molecular trick, the material melts at significantly lower temperatures and remains stable. Studies on cobalt-containing glasses have shown that this gentler process prevents the formation of harmful decomposition products," explains Prof. Dr. Matthias Bauer from Paderborn University.

Preventing these unwanted byproducts is particularly important when studying magnetic properties. Impurities can interfere with measurements and conceal the material's actual magnetic behavior. By keeping the glass chemically stable, the researchers can observe these effects more clearly.

Advanced X-ray Measurements Confirm the Changes

To verify that the molecular treatment genuinely altered the glass, the research team turned to sophisticated analytical techniques.

Studying glass presents a challenge because its atoms do not follow the regular, repeating arrangement found in crystalline materials. This limits what conventional X-ray methods can reveal about its internal structure.

Prof. Bauer explains: "Instead, we used X-ray absorption spectroscopy, amongst other techniques. This method enabled us to investigate the immediate surroundings of the cobalt atoms."

The measurements provided strong evidence that the new molecule changes the arrangement of atoms around the metal centers.

Although the cobalt atoms maintained the same chemical state (oxidation state), their local surroundings changed considerably. The bonds connecting them to nearby molecules were reorganized to accommodate the added phenanthroline.

These observations confirmed that the method does more than simply help the material melt. It changes the underlying chemistry of the glass itself.

A New Generation of Glass With Tunable Properties

The researchers also demonstrated that their approach works beyond the original materials they investigated. Successful experiments with carboxylate-based framework structures suggest that the technique could be applied to a broader range of glass materials.

This versatility is especially promising because it transforms the melting stage of production into an opportunity to design new material properties.

Prof. Henke summarizes the significance for the future: "The melt is no longer a rigid intermediate state. It becomes a reaction space in which we can program the structure."

The ability to precisely modify metal centers could eventually lead to advanced glass components designed for specific technological purposes.

Potential applications include chemical catalysts, sensors, and optoelectronic devices that use interactions between light and electricity. Researchers could also develop materials capable of controlling magnetic behavior, manipulating light, or influencing chemical reactions with greater precision.

By turning molten glass into a material whose chemistry can be deliberately adjusted, the discovery offers a new route toward specialized glasses with properties that conventional manufacturing techniques could not easily produce.

#4386. Goodbye, cavities? Scientists create gel that could regrow tooth enamel

Scientists have developed a new gel that could make it possible to regrow damaged tooth enamel, potentially overcoming one of the biggest limitations in dental care. Unlike bones and many other tissues in the body, tooth enamel cannot naturally regenerate once it has been lost. The new treatment offers a promising way to rebuild this protective layer, strengthen teeth, and help prevent future decay.

The innovation comes from researchers at the University of Nottingham's School of Pharmacy and Department of Chemical and Environmental Engineering. Their new material is inspired by the biological processes that form tooth enamel during early childhood. It is designed to repair enamel that has been weakened by mineral loss or worn away by erosion, while also reinforcing enamel that remains healthy.

The findings, published in Nature Communications, could pave the way for a new generation of dental treatments that go beyond protecting existing enamel and actually help restore its structure.

One of the most promising features of the technology is its simplicity. Dentists could apply the gel directly to teeth using a procedure similar to existing fluoride treatments, making it potentially easy to incorporate into routine dental care.

Unlike conventional fluoride products, however, the new gel contains no fluoride. Instead, it uses a material made from proteins that imitates important characteristics of the natural proteins responsible for guiding enamel formation when teeth first develop.

Once applied, the gel forms a thin but durable coating that penetrates the tooth's surface and fills microscopic cracks and gaps. This coating then provides a framework for rebuilding the mineral structure of enamel.

The process relies on calcium and phosphate ions, two essential mineral components naturally present in saliva. The gel attracts these minerals and helps organize them into new crystals that grow in an orderly pattern.

Scientists call this process epitaxial mineralization. Essentially, it means that new mineral crystals grow in alignment with the existing enamel, allowing the newly formed material to become structurally integrated with the original tooth surface.

This organization is especially important because enamel gets its exceptional hardness and durability from the precise arrangement of its mineral crystals. Simply depositing minerals on a tooth is not enough to recreate the complex structure that makes natural enamel so effective.

By guiding crystal growth, the new gel can restore both the microscopic architecture and the physical properties of healthy enamel.

A Potential Solution for Tooth Sensitivity and Decay

The researchers also discovered that their material can be used on exposed dentine, commonly called dentin in the United States. Dentin is the layer of tooth tissue beneath the enamel. It is softer than enamel and contains tiny channels that can transmit sensations toward the nerves inside the tooth.

When enamel wears away, or gums recede, exposed dentin can make teeth particularly sensitive to hot, cold, sweet, or acidic foods and drinks.

The new gel can encourage the formation of an enamel-like mineral layer over exposed dentin. This could help reduce tooth sensitivity while also improving the attachment of dental restorations, such as fillings and other treatments used to repair damaged teeth.

The potential benefits are significant. Enamel deterioration is a major factor in tooth decay and contributes to dental problems that affect nearly half of the world's population. These conditions can cause pain, infections, and eventually tooth loss. Poor oral health is also associated with broader health problems, including diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

One of the greatest challenges in dentistry is that enamel has no living cells capable of rebuilding it after teeth have fully developed. Although saliva can naturally replace some minerals lost during the earliest stages of enamel damage, the body cannot regenerate substantial amounts of enamel that have been worn away.

Existing treatments, including fluoride varnishes and remineralization products, can help protect teeth and repair early mineral loss. However, they cannot fully reconstruct enamel that has already been lost.

The new technology aims to overcome that limitation by encouraging the formation of new mineral tissue with properties resembling those of the original enamel.

Regenerated Enamel Performs Like Natural Tooth Enamel

The research team tested the mechanical strength and durability of the regenerated material under conditions designed to mimic everyday use.

These experiments examined how the newly formed enamel responded to activities and exposures that teeth routinely experience, including brushing, chewing, and contact with acidic foods.

The results were encouraging. According to the researchers, the regenerated enamel displayed mechanical properties comparable to those of healthy natural enamel, suggesting that the material could provide more than a temporary protective coating.

Dr. Abshar Hasan, a postdoctoral fellow and the study's lead author, explained why recreating enamel's internal structure is so important.

"Dental enamel has a unique structure, which gives enamel its remarkable properties that protect our teeth throughout life against physical, chemical, and thermal insults. When our material is applied to demineralized or eroded enamel, or exposed dentine, the material promotes the growth of crystals in an integrated and organized manner, recovering the architecture of our natural healthy enamel. We have tested the mechanical properties of these regenerated tissues under conditions simulating 'real-life situations' such as tooth brushing, chewing, and exposure to acidic foods, and found that the regenerated enamel behaves just like healthy enamel."

These findings suggest that the gel could eventually offer a way to restore the strength and protective function of damaged enamel rather than simply slowing further deterioration. However, the laboratory results do not yet establish how well the treatment will perform over extended periods in patients.

Beyond its ability to regenerate enamel, the researchers emphasize that the technology was developed with practical dental applications in mind.

The gel is designed to be safe, simple to apply, and suitable for manufacturing on a larger scale. Its versatility could also allow it to be incorporated into several types of dental products, potentially benefiting patients of different ages with enamel erosion, tooth sensitivity, or other problems involving exposed dentin.

Professor Alvaro Mata, Chair in Biomedical Engineering & Biomaterials at the University of Nottingham, led the study and highlighted the potential for translating the discovery into products that dentists can use.

"We are very excited because the technology has been designed with the clinician and patient in mind. It is safe, can be easily and rapidly applied, and it is scalable. Also, the technology is versatile, which opens the opportunity to be translated into multiple types of products to help patients of all ages suffering from a variety of dental problems associated with loss of enamel and exposed dentine. We have started this process with our start-up company Mintech-Bio and hope to have a first product out by next year; this innovation could soon be helping patients worldwide."

The researchers have already begun working toward commercialization through their company, Mintech-Bio, with the goal of introducing an initial product as early as the year following the announcement.

Although further development and clinical validation will be important before the technology becomes an established dental treatment, its ability to recreate the structure and strength of natural enamel represents a promising advance.

If the approach proves successful in patients, it could fundamentally change how dentists address enamel loss, opening the possibility of rebuilding tooth surfaces that previously could only be protected or restored using conventional dental materials.

#4383. A surprising discovery could help aging muscles repair themselves

Muscles can begin losing their strength and ability to recover surprisingly early in the aging process. Over time, muscle tissue may develop scar tissue, accumulate fat, and lose some of the specialized fibers responsible for rapid, powerful movements. These changes can make everyday activities more difficult and gradually reduce mobility and physical independence.

Now, scientists in Japan have identified a promising molecule that could help protect the body's natural muscle repair system and potentially make it more effective. In laboratory experiments, the compound strengthened an important biological signal involved in muscle regeneration, increasing its ability to connect with a key cellular receptor by more than twofold.

The discovery comes from a team led by Professor Ryuichi Tatsumi at Kyushu University's Faculty of Agriculture. Their findings, published in Scientific Reports, suggest a possible new approach to addressing the cellular changes that make aging muscles increasingly difficult to repair.

How Aging Disrupts the Body's Muscle Repair System

Skeletal muscles are the muscles attached to bones that allow us to walk, lift objects, maintain posture, and perform other voluntary movements. Although these muscles experience wear and tear throughout life, they also have a remarkable ability to repair themselves.

Much of that repair depends on specialized stem cells known as satellite cells. These cells normally remain inactive, positioned alongside muscle fibers until they receive a signal that repair or regeneration is needed. Once activated, they can multiply and develop into muscle cells that help restore damaged tissue.

An essential part of this process involves a protein called hepatocyte growth factor, or HGF. Despite its name, HGF plays important roles beyond the liver, including helping activate the stem cells responsible for muscle regeneration.

Under normal conditions, HGF is stored within the supportive material surrounding muscle fibers. When muscles experience an injury or mechanical stimulation, such as physical movement or stretching, the protein can be released.

HGF then attaches to a receptor called c-met on the surface of satellite cells. Receptors are specialized proteins that receive molecular signals and trigger responses inside cells. In this case, the interaction helps awaken dormant satellite cells, allowing them to multiply, mature, and participate in repairing muscle fibers.

But this carefully coordinated system becomes less reliable with age.

A Hidden Chemical Change May Weaken Aging Muscles

The researchers' previous work revealed that HGF can undergo a chemical modification known as nitration. This process attaches a chemical group called a nitro group to particular locations on a protein, potentially changing its structure and interfering with its normal activity.

For HGF, the researchers identified two especially important locations, Y198 and Y250. Both lie within the region involved in attaching to the c-met receptor.

When these sites undergo nitration, HGF becomes less capable of connecting with its receptor. The result is similar to a key that has become damaged and can no longer operate its intended lock.

This disruption could have important consequences for aging muscles. Even if the body continues producing HGF, chemical changes may prevent the protein from properly activating the stem cells needed for tissue repair. The researchers believe this mechanism may contribute to age-related muscle wasting and declining regenerative capacity.

"HGF is not necessarily missing as we age," explains Tatsumi. "Rather, it can be chemically altered after it is made. That led us to wonder whether a compound with strong antioxidant capacity might protect HGF, either by preventing nitration or by compensating for the functional loss it causes."

Scientists Test Two Powerful Sulfur Compounds

To investigate that possibility, the team studied two compounds with strong antioxidant properties: glutathione trisulfide (GSSSG) and lipoic acid trisulfide (LASSS).

Antioxidants can help limit certain types of chemical damage caused by reactive molecules. Such damage can interfere with proteins and other essential components of cells, particularly when the body's normal protective systems become less effective.

The two compounds belong to a chemical family called trisulfides. Their defining feature is a chain of three sulfur atoms connected to one another. This arrangement gives them unusual chemical properties, including an ability to participate in reactions involving the transfer of electrons, known as redox reactions.

Because these reactions play important roles in cellular chemistry, trisulfides have attracted growing interest as potential ingredients in new medicines.

In the first set of experiments, both compounds reduced nitration at the two vulnerable sites on HGF. However, preventing this chemical modification did not completely restore the protein's ability to attach to c-met.

The scientists therefore increased the amount of trisulfide used relative to HGF. They changed the molar ratio, which compares the number of molecules of each substance, from 1:4000 to 1:8000.

That adjustment produced an unexpected result.

An Unexpected Discovery Creates "Super HGF"

At the higher concentration, LASSS did much more than protect HGF from chemical damage. It also dramatically improved the protein's ability to bind to its receptor.

Compared with untreated HGF, the protein exposed to LASSS showed more than twice the binding affinity for c-met. In other words, it could attach to its target receptor much more strongly, potentially enhancing a critical step in the muscle repair process.

The treatment also made HGF more resistant to the loss of function caused by nitration, particularly at the Y198 site.

Notably, the effect was specific to LASSS. Although GSSSG had also reduced nitration in the earlier experiments, it did not produce the same improvement in receptor binding.

"This exceeded our expectations," comments Tatsumi. "We knew trisulfides had diverse biological functions, but we never expected that simply mixing HGF with LASSS would produce such a striking effect.

"What this tells us is that LASSS does more than simply neutralize reactive molecules. It may interact directly with HGF and induce a subtle structural change, creating an enhanced 'Super HGF' form that binds c-met more strongly and resists nitration."

The researchers suspect that LASSS interacts with HGF in a way that slightly alters the protein's three-dimensional shape. Because a protein's shape helps determine how well it interacts with other molecules, even a small structural adjustment could substantially change its activity.

The result is what the team describes as "Super HGF," a potentially enhanced form of the body's existing muscle repair signal.

Importantly, stronger receptor binding does not automatically establish that muscle regeneration itself has improved. Additional experiments will be needed to determine whether this molecular enhancement translates into better muscle healing and strength.

Mouse Experiments Reveal Promising Protection

After observing the effects in laboratory experiments, the researchers wanted to determine whether LASSS could also protect HGF inside living muscle tissue.

They used mice subjected to tail suspension, an established experimental method for studying muscle atrophy. By reducing normal weight bearing and muscle use, this technique produces some of the changes associated with prolonged inactivity, including muscle deterioration.

Mice that received LASSS before the experiment showed significantly less HGF nitration than untreated animals. This suggested that the compound's ability to protect the muscle repair protein was not limited to controlled laboratory conditions.

Once again, GSSSG failed to produce the same protective result.

These findings provide early evidence that LASSS can influence the chemical processes affecting HGF within living animals. However, the mouse experiments demonstrated protection against nitration, not that LASSS restored lost muscle mass or improved physical strength.

The researchers emphasize that studies involving aging animals are still necessary to establish the compound's effectiveness and safety in vivo, meaning within a living organism.

A Potential New Strategy Against Age-Related Muscle Loss

The discovery could eventually contribute to treatments aimed at maintaining muscle function during aging or extended periods of inactivity.

Muscle deterioration is not limited to older adults. It can also occur during prolonged bed rest or other situations in which muscles are used less frequently. When muscle repair mechanisms become impaired, recovering lost strength and function can become especially challenging.

Rather than replacing the body's natural repair machinery, the approach explored in this study seeks to protect and enhance an existing biological signal. If the benefits can be confirmed in future studies, strengthening HGF activity could become one strategy for supporting muscle regeneration.

The scientists also believe that the underlying effects of LASSS on HGF may extend across species. That raises the possibility of applications not only in human medicine but also in veterinary care, particularly for aging companion animals such as dogs and cats.

For now, the findings represent an early step toward understanding how a naturally occurring muscle repair pathway might be strengthened. Whether LASSS can safely and effectively preserve muscle function during aging remains an open question.

Still, the unexpected discovery that a sulfur-based compound can both protect and enhance a critical repair protein offers a promising direction for future research, with the long-term goal of helping people maintain mobility, independence, and a better quality of life as they grow older.

#4380. 10 Details That Show Rockstar Went Above and Beyond With GTA VI

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Rockstar has made some amazing games over the years, and one thing that always remains the same is that the team has an amazing attention to detail. The maps are massive, full of life, have tons of activities, and even have insane levels of detail that you would never even think to look at.

A small instance of this can be seen in Arthur Morgan, as his hair grows, can be cut, and even styled. It is easy to see why Rockstar often gets praise from gamers. However, now it is time for GTA VI to shine.

Like before, Rockstar has definitely gone above and beyond with the attention to detail, and this is just part of the reason why GTA VI is a great game.

Ah yes, just when I am trying to get any work done, I turn to my phone, pick it up, and start flipping through social media. Specifically, I start swiping through shorts on YouTube or reels on Instagram.

If you are addicted to doomscrolling through life like many people in the world, the good news is that you can do that in GTA VI. Rockstar has never shied away from emulating life in some aspects of each of their games, and this time, you can use the Snapmatic app in GTA VI to scroll through posts and viral clips.

Of course, this has a connection to the actual gameplay, and no, you can’t become a viral star in GTA VI, but it does show the level of detail Rockstar is going for in the game, as the feed gets updated. Just don’t doomscroll very long.

The wanted system has evolved over the years that the Grand Theft Auto series has existed, but it has never been this detailed. Previously, if you became wanted, you could simply hide, wait out the cops, and leave when they forget you exist.

Now, the cops remember you. They know what you look like, whether you were with a partner, what car you drive, and the clothes you wear. Each of these gets marked, and you need to take care of them if you want to avoid detection.

If they know your outfit, you need to change. If they know your car, you need to get a new one. If you don’t wear a mask, they will know your face. It is a level of detail never seen in the wanted system.

Grand Theft Auto V had a decent number of buildings you could enter, with the total being roughly around 100. Still, when you are living in a city, that number is pretty small and mostly impressive by game standards.

Grand Theft Auto VI takes this to a new level, and it shows how dedicated Rockstar is to going above and beyond with detail, as it is estimated that 70% of the buildings are enterable. The confirmed number by the mapping community based on trailers and available data is sitting at around 400, that is already over four times the number in the previous game.

It is amazing that Rockstar has taken the time and energy to put in so many details and fully flesh out all of these buildings.

GTA Online 2.0 will be coming eventually, and there are some changes that Rockstar should make.

Leonida is based on Florida, and if you have ever been to Florida, you know that there is a lot of wildlife there. Venture outside of the city, and you can find numerous animals living in the wetlands.

Rockstar made sure to go above and beyond when it comes to the game’s animals with the team putting in more than 170 different animal species. This includes over 60 bird species, 30 land mammals, and also various aquatic life and reptiles.

For context, Grand Theft Auto V has around 28 different animal species, and Red Dead Redemption 2 has over 200. Leonida will be just as wild as the real Florida.

The Grand Theft Auto series obviously has a large emphasis on committing crimes, with each game giving you the ability to rob stores, steal cars, and more. However, none of the previous titles have the same level of detail when it comes to committing a crime.

GTA VI has multiple options when committing a crime. Will you wear a mask? Do you want to bring a partner? Are you going to use a silencer on your weapon? This all plays into whether you get caught in the act and how the police respond.

On top of this, other crimes like stealing a car are now more detailed as well, with you having the ability to bust windows or even use tools to pop locks. Some cars even have trackers. You can even use an app to determine a car’s resale value.

It is easy to overlook NPCs in a video game unless you are directly interacting with them. All the people on the street tend to blur together at times, but when you stop to take a look, you will see various NPCs that look alike.

In GTA V, it is estimated that there are around 800 unique NPCs roaming the streets of Los Santos and beyond. However, when tested, players have shown it doesn’t take very long to run into the same NPC but in a different location.

Let’s scale this up to GTA VI. There isn’t an official number yet, but Rockstar has stated that the NPCs will be far more diverse, with they varying in height and weight. They will also have defining details like birthmarks, moles, skin conditions, and more. Even the sizes of their muscles, butts, and chests can differ. That’s a lot of detail.

The weather often gets crazy down in Florida. It is normal for residents of the state to deal with torrential downpours, strong winds, tropical storms, and even hurricanes. In other words, you can’t expect Leonida to not have similar weather.

GameInformer detailed some of the weather effects that will be in GTA VI, and according to them, there will be tropical storms and hurricanes that make “water gush off roof edges and lamposts,” and make it so “everything is dripping wet.”

This means that you will need to unleash your inner Florida Man and run through a hurricane to see what happens. Maybe you will get tossed around. I just hope Rockstar captured the downpour that seems to happen every day around 3pm.

GTA 6 features a completely rebuilt dynamic wind and atmospheric system designed to bring the tropical world of Leonida to life like never before.

Being a Rockstar game, there is a degree of change that can be expected to happen to your character. This didn’t exist in GTA V, but in Red Dead Redemption 2, Arthur Morgan’s weight could change, his hair could grow and be cut, and his face changes.

Rockstar has taken this a step further for GTA VI, as you have two protagonists, and both of them can have their appearance change over time. Overeating causes weight gain, undereating causes weight loss, working out makes your muscles grow, and much more.

The protagonists aren’t just static characters that don’t change with time, they evolve and grow. Their hair also grows and needs to be cut. This level of detail is above and beyond what happens in a normal game.

While GTA V is great, the NPCs in that game are pretty lackluster. When you commit a crime, they mostly switch between two actions; fight or run. Mostly, they run away from guns, car crashes, or whatever else.

The NPCs in GTA VI, however, act much differently. They are more lifelike. They will take out their phones to record you. You can listen in on conversations, and the NPCs will get angry if they spot you. The NPCs will go so far as to remember you.

This means that if you continuously wreak havoc in Leonida, the NPCs will act differently towards you. Some may even be hostile as soon as they see you. A lot of work goes into making NPCs feel lifelike, and Rockstar is going above and beyond with it.

If it wasn’t obvious already, GTA VI is about a couple named Lucia and Jason. The pair are trying to create a better life and get out of crime. A big part of the game revolves around their relationship.

The couple can spend time together, furthering their bond. They can play games like mini-golf, go scuba diving together, and much more. The more they spend time together, the stronger their bond will become.

Rockstar put a lot of detail in just the relationship aspect of the game, with your partner messaging you throughout the day to check in and more. You actually need to care about who you commit crime with, as if you don’t your relationship will fail and affect the story.

The Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks have revealed some interesting details about the game, such as new mechanics and changes to the menus.
