#4283. Battlefield 6's latest update dubbed the game's simultaneously best and worst patch as it runs into all kinds of issues

What's likely going to be the last major Battlefield 6 update of the year has launched with a number of unexpected issues.

There’s been a lot of anticipation for Battlefield 6’s version 1.1.3.0 patch. The patch kicks off the third and final phase of the game’s first season, adding some new holiday-themed content. More the new content itself, the update’s biggest additions are almost entirely gameplay-related.

Unfortunately, for as much as the changes in 1.1.3.0 have been well received, the launch has been marred by a series of technical issues, some of which are a little unusual.

Immediately after patch 1.1.3.0 went live, players on PC started reporting massive stutters that would occur every few seconds. The issue is especially pronounced in Redsec Battle Royale, but much deadlier in traditional multiplayer.

Battlefield Studios quickly acknowledged it, pointing out a workaround that appears to be working for players on Steam. According to those players, going offline on Steam’s friends menu has fixed stuttering for them.

The issue remains for other players on PC, however, and the developer said it’s working on a proper fix.

Perhaps the most disrupting problem the patch has caused is one that prevents players from being able to interact with the game’s menu. Tiles become unresponsive, or outright unselectable when you try to hover near them.

Ironically, the top set of tiles designed to make it easy for players to quickly jump into the new content has been the most affected. Restarting the game sometimes fixes the issue, and some players report that it only happens upon first launch after installing the update.

But Battlefield Studios later clarified that, unsurprisingly, there’s an actual reason behind the bug. Once again, a fix is being investigated, and the developer will offer an update once some progress has been made.

A little further down the list of importance is an issue that stops players from being able to skip tiers within the new Winter Offensive bonus path in the game’s battle pass. BF Studios took out the feature entirely while it works on a fix, so while you can continue making progress in the bonus path, you won’t be able to skip tiers.

This is all a shame to see. Outside of all the problems, the meat of the new update has been almost universally praised. The visibility improvements, and netcode updates have been celebrated. Many players were also happy to see meaningful updates to footstep audio and overall clarity.

It’s also unusual for a Battlefield 6 patch to run into so many issues at launch. The sentiment around 1.1.3.0 so far is that it’s the game’s best and worst update yet. Hopefully those issues will be fixed before the development team breaks for the holidays.

#4282. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – October 30, 2026

Welcome to Devil's Night, the night before Halloween, where video games are best served scary. After tomorrow night – Halloween proper – no more scary video games allowed. At least not until mid-September, 2027. I'm sorry, I don't make the rules. Below you will find our weekend gaming recommendations (which is actually surprisingly light on scary games – apologies), but before that, here are some of the biggest stories of the week.

Phantom Blade Zero is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, and it’s certainly one of the most impressive to watch. Beijing-based developer S-Game uses China’s Wuxia brand of action (which was actually banned for some time during the 20th Century by the country’s government) to create a stylish, fluid, and hyper-engaging combat system. It will constantly leave you in awe that action combat can look this good. But looks aren’t everything. Fortunately, Phantom Blade Zero delivers on all fronts, with weapon mechanics so detailed that picking up a new blade can feel like unlocking a new character in a fighting game. The story won’t blow your socks off, but it’s certainly engaging and enticing enough to bring you through Phantom Blade Zero’s 40 or so hours of content. If you’re not interested in the “perfect ending,” which is the only satisfactory one in my opinion, you can complete the game in less than 30 hours. S-Game mixes high-octane combat with sprawling and rewarding exploration to create a must-play during this already busy season of games. You can read more of my thoughts in the Game Informer Phantom Blade Zero review, and if you are hopping in this weekend, be sure to check out my list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks I wish I knew before starting it.

If you have any fond memories of IllFonic’s ill-fated Friday the 13th: The Game as I do, you simply must play the studio’s latest, Halloween: The Game. It is essentially Friday the 13th with Michael Myers instead of Jason, but with a decade of lessons learned from the team’s teeth carving in other horror properties and games. You’re either Michael or a citizen; the former wants to kill you and all the NPCs in various suburban maps, while the latter must rescue as many NPCs as possible while staying alive themselves. It’s that classic cat-and-mouse formula IllFonic is the master of, but with all the style, substance, and synths of John Carpenter’s Halloween masterpiece. Plus, Halloween: The Game features IllFonic’s first crack at a single-player campaign, and while it’s largely a tutorial for playing as Michael, if you’re a Halloween mega-fan like me, it’s worth checking out if only to take part in some of the film’s most iconic kills. You can read more of my thoughts in the Game Informer Halloween: The Game review here, and if you’re hopping in this weekend, there’s a new map, additional Halloween-themed cosmetics to unlock, and more waiting for you.

Overwatch is in the midst of its Halloween event, which have always historically been pretty interesting. This year it's Mystery Madness: Graveyard Games. In it, you begin by picking one of three characters in a random role. And then, as the game progresses, you choose perks that upgrade, alter, or completely change what your character can do. It can get really chaotic where by round three characters like Orisa might be three times her normal size or Torbjorn might have placed a giant turret on Mercy's making her a flying death machine. There are also Halloween skins, as well.

Tom the Postgirl is an odd little adventure that I'd recommend to fans of Untitled Goose Game. You play as Tom, a creepy girl who's tasked with delivering packages to the people of her wacky town, which is depicted with storybook-style illustrations and a color palette limited to black, white, and red. On the surface, you're delivering packages, but the game's real story is based on Tom's tendency to peep where she shouldn't, peering into townsfolks' windows to watch their odd lives. On house is full of kids who live like dogs; another has a couple with a bizarre obsession with tickling. You never know what each window might reveal, and I quickly sympathized with (and enabled) Tom's compulsion. You also have the capacity to cause quite a bit of trouble by stomping on flowers, haphazardly snipping strings and cords, or even stealing packages and using them for your own mischievous purposes. It's a pretty short experience, completable in just a few hours, making it a nice palate cleanser between the massive releases at the end of the year.

This Devolver Digital-published game has a simple but head-turning premise. You’re a profoundly angry woman who returns to her small hometown armed with nothing but a sledgehammer, which she uses to smash everything in sight. The town is also inhabited by robots possessing human consciousnesses. Swinging the hammer can either punch holes through walls or, with enough force, reduce entire buildings to rubble. But why is she doing this? Why is she so mad? A big part of Virtue and a Sledgehammer’s allure is its fascinating and well-written tale about the protagonist’s strained relationships with her sister and mother. Learning more about their lives requires you to keep smashing, but the more you learn, the more you begin to question whether smashing everything is actually a good idea.

This bizarre indie blends fun match-3 puzzle-solving with tower defense gameplay wrapped around a funny but surreal story. The match-3 gameplay involves sliding tiles to match geographic elements like castles, trees, and rivers to collect resources that feed into the tower defense portion. Depending on how the board looks when the puzzle portion ends, you send troops (sustained by the resources you collected) to attack/defend against rival castles and gather more items; board positioning determines how well this can go. The two mechanics feed into each other to create a fun loop that grows in complexity as new mechanics are introduced. Did I mention the game is also very weird? The silly tale centers on a medieval court designating you the chosen savior to rescue their lost queen (and many other tasks), and the dumb tone adds personality to a sometimes dry genre. Titanium Court charmed and impressed us when it launched on PC earlier this year, and now console and mobile players get their chance to hold court.

Sword of the Sea is a beautiful, 2025 game about surfing through the sand atop a floating sword. It recalls Journey, the emotional 2012 PlayStation game, which makes sense as it comes from the artists and developers that worked on that game, developer Giant Squid. Giant Squid also made 2016's Abzû and 2020's The Pathless. It's a talented team and Sword of the Sea maintains that reputation. And now you can play it on Switch 2. You can read my full review of the game (though this review pertains to the PlayStation 5 version) right here.

Cities: Skylines arrived on PC more than a decade ago, but is still revered as one of the greatest modern city-builders. Even now, three years after the sequel's release, Paradox continues supporting and porting the original game. A couple years after its initial release, Cities: Skylines received a strong console port, which did an admirable job of adapting the controls to gamepads, but the Switch version was always the weakest of the bunch. As of this week, Switch 2 owners can play a less compromised version, expanding the Switch's 9-tile limit to a much larger 25-tile limit, as well as better performance and textures, better control panels, and a ton of DLC and added content. And on top of that, if you own the Switch 1 version, you get a deep discount on the Switch 2 version.

While not specifically about this new Switch 2 version, you can read our original reviews of the base PC version here, and the base console version here.

Minecraft has held its dominant spot in pop culture for so long that it's easy to forget a simple fact about it: the game is awesome. This week, it's coming to Switch 2, giving potential miners another platform to explore procedurally-generated caves in. You've certainly heard of it, and you've probably played it, but I still feel it often doesn't get the flowers it deserves in high-level critical discussions about games, despite its regular cadence of major updates. The opening gameplay loop is so satisfying that for many of my peers, whether they regularly play video games or not, it's only a matter of time before they boot up a new world again. While you can never play the game for the first time again, if you haven't checked it out in a couple years, you might be surprised by the amount of new blocks, materials, and mobs they've added in recent updates. And if you've never played before, the Switch 2 launch is as good a time as any to see what all the fuss is about.

The card game incarnation of Arkham Horror remains one of the best narrative-driven and horror-themed tabletop games around, and it's an easy recommendation if you're looking for something engaging to dive into on Halloween night. Rooted in the monsters and mysteries of the Cthulhu Mythos, this living card game is built on major core sets and expansions. But unlike a TCG, each new installment has the same cards included, fueling the cooperative adventures you'll undertake together with your fellow players. Last year Arkham Horror: The Card Game did something of a soft relaunch for a chapter 2 of its narrative, and that new core set is an ideal place to jump on  play. Players each control an individual investigator as they explore arcane and weird mysteries, confront monsters, and unfold plots of cultists, ancient entities, and forbidden lore. For fans of cosmic horror storytelling, it's an easy pick.

#4281. Murals Interview: How To Create A Mascot Who's Not As Annoying As Ocarina Of Time's Navi

Scott Baird is a Contributor from the UK with over a decade of video game writing experience.

Murals is an upcoming action RPG by Dlala Studios that, on the surface, looks a great deal like Hades. The concept of Murals involves twisted and humorous takes on classic fairy tales, like Rapunzel, which is an idea that’s more commonplace than the straight tellings of those stories, with everyone from Disney to Alan Moore turning fables on their head.

Originality isn’t the golden ticket to a video game being enjoyable, and in this case, the differences from genre norms are in the gameplay, not the story. While Murals might look like countless isometric action RPG roguelikes on Steam, it’s going for a linear, narrative-based progression, with crafted levels and enemies, rather than relying on randomness.

Playing it straight is a surprisingly bold move, and it runs counter to the story of Murals. DualShockers recently visited Dlala’s offices to preview Murals, where we got the chance to speak to the studio’s CEO, AJ Grand-Scrutton, about the many choices that went into making Murals.

Q: The idea of fables and fairy tales being twisted and viewed through a modern lens has been done many times before. Were there any specific examples that inspired Murals?

Grand-Scrutton: So obviously the source material was where we went to initially, the grim stuff and the Hans Christian Andersen. But I mean, I loved American McGee's Alice. I was a massive fan of that. There's a lot of like comic books as well, like Fables. I love Wolf Among Us. So I love that familiarity that you recognize the story, but enough difference that you don't feel you're just retreading old ground.

Q: Have any video games inspired the gameplay or design of Murals?

Grand-Scrutton: Obviously, Murals is isometric and it's got pretty chaotic moment to moment. So a lot of modern Roguelikes, your Hades, et cetera. I struggle with permadeath, especially as I've got older. I'm quite impatient and moody. And so kind of what I really loved was like the moment to moment in a lot of modern roguelikes, but I didn't necessarily get on very well with the permadeath loop. So that was a big influence for how Murals came about.

Like, can we take some of those chaotic moment to moment experiences; those combat augmentation systems and deliver them in like a bit longer form content? And also like, you know, weird influences in there as well. You know, like a lot of our world building Psychonauts and a lot of double fine stuff was really prominent in our minds. And, you know, classic combat games like DMC, Bayonetta.

But yeah, it was really just about us trying to capture an experience we didn't feel we could fully play out there already.

We traveled to China to chat with Soulframe about his upcoming action RPG, Phantom Blade Zero.

Q: The protagonist is mostly silent in Murals, with most of the talking being done by the character’s sidekick, Loaf. How do you go about designing a talkative side character like Loaf in a way that makes them likeable. Were there any concerns they’d become another Navi from Ocarina of Time?

Grand-Scrutton: Yeah, so, I mean, we always are very aware that our style of writing can become... Every character can feel like that very quickly for people. I mean, I think if you look at Battletoads, you look at Illusion Island and you look at Murals, you can tell it's very much like the same writing team that have done them.

Loaf is kind of, in a weird way, is obviously this sentient sketch come to life. He's the most naturally written character because it's often me and Kelsy, my lead writer, just typing what we're thinking about situations or stupid commets. Like, often we'll just be on calls and we'll play through the game. And Kelsy, as well as writing, she actually is Loaf. She does the voice of Loaf. And we'll almost do our own little director's commentaries as we're playing the game to figure out where Loaf comments should go and what would Loaf say in this situation.

I think with humour, comedy in games, we're not unique. There's other people that do comedy games, but it's still quite a niche. And I think you kind of just have to lean into what you are. And I think that we are that self-referential type of humour. We do the fourth wall breaking. There is the modern label of the meta-level stuff in there. And I think it'd be easy for us to go half-arsed or half-cocked on it. But we just kind of leant into it. This is what we find funny, and that's kind of how we write the game.

Q: Why go for such a basic, sketch outline design for Loaf?

Grand-Scrutton: Yeah, I love the juxtaposition. So obviously, as you've seen from the couple of murals you've played, the characters that live in the world are hand-animated, but they've still got depth to them.

The invasive forces, which is the distorted, the enemies, and the hero, the player, are fully animated. And I love this idea that Loaf was just... the hero just made this rough sketch in their notebook or something and accidentally got brought to life. I love Doodlebob, who is definitely an influence from the SpongeBob cartoons.

I just think there's something really nice about... we've got these animated characters that are still not realistic, but almost like they make sense. And then Loaf is just a cartoon. He doesn't really have the rules of physicality that a humanoid would have. He is just who he is. And I think that just gave us some really fun opportunities, and it let us do some silly things with him.

An interview with Jonathan Blow about the making and future of Order of the Sinking Star.

Q: Is Murals intended as a linear experience, or is there more of a roguelike/Hades-style progression, with a hub area, random layouts, and upgrades sticking between runs.

Grand-Scrutton: No, it's very, very linear. Like, we're always up front about that because we know how misleading it can be when you see like an isometric action game. It's very linear. Like, the only real elements of random to it are the order you get the Eeries in.

So, you know, if you do a playthrough, you may get different Eeries to someone else doing the exact same playthrough. But the story, the quests, the enemies themselves, that is all very sculpted.

Q: In the Murals preview, there’s a very generous window for being able to dash out of attacks. Is this planned to be maintained for the final build or is the gameplay balance being tweaked still, out of fear it could make the combat too easy?

Grand-Scrutton: Yes, no, maybe to all the above. We're still tweaking. We'll be tweaking until my Tech Director pries it from my cold dead hands. We definitely have gone generous with a lot of things like this. I think the difficulty you're playing in general is probably on the easier side of what we would balance the final game.

You know, we're looking to make it customizable though, right? In terms of like enemy health, enemy damage, amount of health, you probably notice in the build you're playing right now that you always have enough health drops to get full health basically. That would probably be the generous setting on the slider for health drops. But I think the dash serves a very specific purpose in our game, obviously it's not unique at all.

But we've got a lot of boss fights, environmental hazards and other enemies as you progress through the game where giving the players a generous dash meant we could get more chaotic with the experience. I think, you know, if you look at our game and compare to some of our other peers, I think that's one of the slight difference of our moment to moment.

I think we're not a one versus one experience. We're not one versus many. We're like a one versus some is what I like to say. But we do reasonably small spaces with a reasonably large amount of enemies. And so while the play space is quite chaotic, we wanted to give the player simple enough verbs that they could control so they never felt like the game was being unfair.

DualShockers spoke with the developers of Wo Long 2: Wings of Ember about why a sequel was made and how the gameplay has changed from its predecessor.

Q: Some of the enemies have a flashing light before they attacked. Is this hinting at a parry mechanic for the full version of the game? Do you dare release a game in 2027 with no parrying?

Grand-Scrutton: I mean, we are daring to not release. No, there's no parry. They're very generous tells on some of the enemies that do more damage. We definitely discussed parrying really early on. We discussed parrying, we discussed blocking. But it just, it felt a bit like a hat on a hat for what we were making. Like, you know, we like, we believe in like, depth through simplicity. This is not a big combo based game.

You know, it's not even as combo laden as like our Battletoads was. It's a very simple amount of inputs with like varying weapons and a lot of depth comes through the power-ups. And the problem I find with parrying is like, modern games are amazing.

Like, you know, Expedition 33, all these games are absolutely outstanding. I find when I play them that my gameplay just becomes around parrying. All I do is parry. Like, in a lot of ways, although I love them, I play them multiple times.

I felt that learning to do the block timing in the Arkham games made the combat a little bit less exciting for me because I actually certainly changed my entire strategy in those games to be let the enemy come to me. And I just didn't want that for this. I didn't want the focus to be on parry timing. I wanted the focus to just be like, have a little bit of fun controlled chaos.

Q: Finally, why choose Murals as the game’s name?

Grand-Scrutton: Yeah, we are traditionally, not necessarily publicly, very awful at doing project codenames. Like, the codename for Battletoads was Frogspawn, which is not the most... And the codename for Illusion Island was Illusions because we weren't originally going to call it that.

So Project Murals was the codename for Murals because we love the idea that these worlds are like these fairy tales brought to life by through these painted murals the creator has done. But the team will tell you, I have this obsession, I think Pokémon is the greatest name for a franchise ever because I love a name that is memorable and it's also the name of a thing in the game or in the world. And I love the idea of us having murals because the levels are called murals and it's also the name and it makes sense.

So it's kind of like this dragon I've been chasing and it just fit the game and it worked for me. And there's some funniness in there as well to me through some previous titles we've worked on and stuff in the past where we've tried to put forward names for things and we've been told that the majority of the...

We had a game we were working on years ago, years and years ago, and it was around animatronics. And this was years back. I mean, it was before it was necessarily common lingo but I really wanted to call it Tronics and I was like, oh, how cool is this name? And we got told by our partners at the time that no one knows what an animatronic is so we couldn't do it. And then Five Nights at Freddy's came out a year later and I was like, everyone knows what animatronic is, look.

And we've had similar things with this, like when we'd kind of pitched this to people before the name Murals, people were like, I don't think anyone's gonna really know what a mural is. And I was like, I'm pretty sure people know what a mural is. So it was nice to kind of have that control ourselves.

The development team behind Disgaea Mayhem discusses balancing an action RPG while maintaining insane level and damage numbers.

#4280. Logitech's Game Day gives employees a day off to play video games

If you've been keeping up with gaming news in recent weeks, you've probably noticed growing speculation about the number of gamers planning to take time off work to binge-play GTA VI when it launches on November 19th.

And whilst there's no shortage of news outlets highlighting the potential economic downside of this mass gaming exodus, one particularly renowned gaming company is looking at the positives.

In recognition of the positive cognitive and professional benefits gaming can provide, Logitech International has announced Logi Game Day, a dedicated day off for its employees to play games. The initiative follows findings from the tech giant's recent Logitech Ctrl Tomorrow study, which revealed that 81% of gamers believe gaming builds real-world confidence, reduces anxiety and correlates with stronger day-to-day work performance.

Alongside the company-wide day off, Logitech G will also host a streaming event at its Americas headquarters in San Jose to celebrate the occasion. And, rather conveniently, it'll take place on November 19th. Isn't it nice how things work out?

A separate study conducted by Logitech also found that 98.8% of enterprise IT decision-maker (ITDM) respondents believe gaming skills translate directly into workplace capabilities, including strategic thinking, complex problem-solving and performing under pressure.

These findings prompted Logitech's chief executive officer, Hanneke Faber, to declare: "It's time to retire the stereotype that gaming is a waste of time. As a company designing products for work and play, we see every day how engagement in one sphere supports performance in the other."

Logitech G's general manager, Robin Piispanen, who'll be hosting the Logi Game Day event, also highlighted the team-building benefits of gaming: "Whether diving into a game like GTA VI or Call of Duty Modern Warfare 4, shaving seconds off lap times in Forza, or teaming up in an online battle, Game Day gives our team a shared purpose," he says. "We see firsthand how Logitech employees who sharpen their skills in-game translate directly back to work and problem-solving."

"Play is not the opposite of work," said Elaine Laird, Logitech's chief people officer. "When people have dedicated time to log off, decompress and immerse themselves in play, they return with clearer focus, renewed energy and fresh approaches to complex challenges."

While it would be somewhat premature to suggest that companies across every industry will eventually embrace similar initiatives, Logitech's decision does reflect a changing attitude towards the positive role gaming can play in our everyday lives. And, as the saying goes, great things have small beginnings.

So here’s hoping that when GTA VII rolls around somewhen in the 2040’s, we’ll all be enjoying a dedicated Game Day without having to call in sick!

#4279. Arc Raiders gets a few map exploit fixes in latest patch as Embark prepares to slow down how often patches are released

There's a new Arc Raiders patch that's fairly small, but one with fixes everyone is going to appreciate.

The time has arrived for another Arc Raiders update, and Embark has certainly delivered. Today’s patch, version 1.6.0, is among the smallest the game has received so far, focusing almost exclusively on disabling map exploits.

Perhaps more important than the patch itself, however, is the announcement the developer made around it.

Starting off with patch 1.6.0, it takes out a particular zipline on Stella Montis, the game’s most recent addition ot the map roster. Some players used said zipline to get out of bounds, something the game has been battling on several of its maps.

On Blue Gate, the patch fixes a collision issue that allowed players to vault through a wall, and fall to their death. The map fixes continue with another on Spaceport Launch Tower, which takes out a gap in collision that players have been able to shoot through.

The last change in this update affects gameplay feel around Arc enemies. Certain materials in the game’s world weren’t blocking their vision - or fire - when they should have, and this has now been fixed.

Alongside today’s patch, Embark also announced that going forward, we’re going to see fewer patches for Arc Raiders. The game has been getting updates almost every Thursday since it launched in late October.

Now that most of the major problems have been fixed, the studio is shifting to a slower patching cadence. Critical fixes will still be issued as soon as they’re developed, but don’t expect a patch each week going forward.

Embark also revealed that patch releases and in-game store rotations will now occur on Tuesdays. You should also expect the next few weeks to be quiet, as members of the team go on holiday breaks.

But, before everyone goes away, the game is going to get one more big update. The last item on Arc Raiders’ roadmap, revealed in early November, is the Cold Snap event. This is on track for Tuesday, bringing some new content alongside a few other fixes.

#4277. Aurora Gaming sweep Pixel Lumina to reach Europe Qualifier 1 final after BONK disqualification

Aurora Gaming beat Pixel Lumina 2-0 to reach the Europe Qualifier 1 final, days after the UK side that had knocked them out was disqualified for cheating. The final decides seeding for the Europe Qualifier Playoffs, the next step towards VCT EMEA Kickoff 2027 in Berlin.

Aurora Gaming will play in the Europe Qualifier 1 final. Their best-of-three semi-final against Pixel Lumina began at 16:00 on Tuesday. Aurora took the opening map in 41 minutes and closed out the second in 35 minutes.

The win completes a turnaround for a side that had already been eliminated from the qualifier. Their earlier exit had come against BONK.

The fallout reached beyond the bracket. Every BONK player and registered participant was also provisionally suspended, GINX TV reported.

The disqualification forced a rework of the schedule. Riot had set Qualifier 1 for 5 to 8 November as a single-elimination, best-of-three bracket. The Pixel Lumina semi-final and the final were pushed back to make room for the rebuilt bracket. All three affected organisations agreed to the new timetable.

Pixel Lumina, a team based in Hungary, came into the match at rank 120 in the Elo power rankings. They hold a rating of 1559 and a 30-28 record across 58 rated matches. Aurora are unranked. Before this semi-final, Pixel Lumina lost to CGN Esports in the VCL EMEA Last Chance Qualifier 2026. That defeat followed wins over FOKUS and Twisted Saints Esports in the same event.

Aurora’s lineup features Boo, chiwa, Derke, B1SK and trexx. Derke joined straight after Valorant Champions 2026, where his Vitality side lost the grand final 3-1 to LOUD.

Aurora now face the winner of xXxMasterProMegaTeamxXx versus F9 EICAR. That final decides seeding for the Kickoff Qualifier Playoffs. Aurora are already listed as qualified for the playoffs through Qualifier 1, so the final is about position rather than survival.

The wider prize is a place at VCT EMEA Kickoff 2027. Europe will supply half of the four non-partner sides heading to the event, Riot Games said, while Türkiye and MENA each send a single team. Kickoff itself will be played offline at the Riot Games Arena in Berlin with 12 teams.

The rest of the European field is still taking shape. Europe Qualifier 2 is scheduled for 12 to 15 November and is also played as single-elimination best-of-three brackets.

#4274. Murals Preview: Frantic Fairy Tale Fun

Murals is taking old fairy tales and filtering them through an action RPG lens, while injecting the stories with a fresh dose of British humor.

Fairy tales have been deconstructed and shown through a modern lens so many times that subversions are almost as common as straight tellings of the original stories. Murals is an upcoming action RPG that takes a comedic, subversive look at classic kids' stories, wrapped in an addictive gameplay loop familiar to fans of the big hits of the past few years.

Roguelike action RPGs have exploded in popularity, especially on PC, with gamers becoming hooked on brutally difficult gameplay merged with random elements that offer near-infinite replayability. On the surface, Murals seems cut from the same cloth as something like Hades, being an action RPG with an isometric viewpoint, where a long hero dashes around, avoiding attacks, while unleashing an increasingly larger arsenal at their foes.

DualShockers visited developer Dlala Studios at their home base for a hands-on preview of Murals. This consisted of playing the first two chapters and experiencing an in-development build of the game that is still being tweaked and worked on. What’s here is impressive, especially in terms of the aesthetics, with gorgeous visuals on display for Murals’ fairy-tale world.

The Murals preview I played featured two stages: Little Briar Rose (the story that formed the basis for Sleeping Beauty), and Rapunzel. The story starts with the protagonist, whose appearance can best be described as “Player 2 April O’Neil,” waking up in a mysterious new world with no memory of how they got there.

The protagonist of Murals doesn't talk much, but when they do, they have branching dialogue options. Sadly, the game immediately says that these have no bearing on the gameplay and are just for flavor, so the choices may as well not exist. While I'm not expecting some Mass Effect-style consequences for every dialogue choice, it'd be nice if some of the responses had some kind of bearing on the gameplay.

The protagonist doesn't talk much because they're soon joined by Loaf, the game's mascot character. Loaf is a poorly drawn doodle that resembles an eraser with lizard-like plates on its back. Loaf quickly sets the comedic tone of the story, with Monty Python-esque retorts to the silliness of their situation, before the two are joined by Slash Gordon, the player’s trusty blade.

The chapters of Murals I experienced involved solving the locals' problems, such as helping an insomniac Sleeping Beauty or freeing a trapped Rapunzel by climbing her hair up the tower. There was also an overarching story involving a mysterious being known as The Creator, who looks like a smug art critic and seems to pull the strings from afar, guiding the protagonist along.

Twisted Tower is a terrifyingly twisted fairy tale that's done its homework.

One reliable ally the player has between battles is Magic Dave, voiced by legendary UK comedian Bob Mortimer. He’s the Resident Evil 4 Merchant of the game, providing upgrades (called Eeries) between stages, while exchanging witty banter with Toast.

The comedy in Murals is going to be love it or hate it. Saying it’s steeped in British irreverence is an understatement, and that sentence alone might be off-putting to some. A great comparison is the works of the late great Terry Pratchett: that provides a metric of Britishness the player should expect.

Dlala Studios is no stranger to pretty 2D games, having previously created the modern Battletoads game, as well as Disney Illusion Island. Murals marks the studio's departure from established intellectual properties and into publishing, which is why fairy tales were the company's next stop, since they're in the public domain.

Easily the high point of Murals is its visuals. Each level in Murals is a stunning, hand-drawn piece of artwork, where every room appears lovingly crafted and filled with little touches to admire while exploring.

Each level in Murals is a stunning, hand-drawn piece of artwork, with every room lovingly crafted and filled with little touches to admire while exploring. The same is true of the character artwork, with everything polished to perfection. The level of detail is especially impressive, considering Murals is still being developed, yet the team already has the aesthetic nailed down.

What once started out as a subgenre of NES classics has now become a typically hand-drawn set of video games that never fail to impress.

The only exception to the pretty visuals is the enemies in Murals, which are 3D models and nowhere near as visually impressive as the stages or NPCs. The monsters are quite generic and don't feel like they match the fairy-tale world they exist in, with designs that could fit into pretty much any action RPG.

The boss monsters are similarly whelming, with the giant frog faced in the Little Briar Rose stage doing the same jumping attack over and over again, only adding mobs to his move pool. In contrast, the final encounter of the Rapunzel stage is just waves of enemies, with no big boss in sight.

Fairy tales are full of creative villains who could be repurposed for use in video games. Just look at The Wolf Among Us for only one example among many. The enemies in Murals need an injection of creativity in both their design and battle strategy if the game wants to keep the player's interest.

It's impossible to play Murals and not compare it to Hades or its sequel. Just looking at a gameplay video on the Steam page, the comparisons are easy to see. It’s impossible to deny that Murals has Hades DNA, with the same basic combat loop, even though it takes a drastically different approach.

In Murals, the player has a choice of melee weapons (the sword named Slash Gordon and the hammer called the Wolfhammer in the demo), a ranged weapon with recharging ammo, and a super move that builds up over the battle, all of which are used to destroy foes. The player can dash to avoid enemy attacks and must survive waves of enemies through chains of rooms, with liberal health drops between areas.

As someone who was brutalized by Hades 2 in the past, one mechanic in Murals' combat immediately stuck out. When swinging a weapon or using a ranged attack, it's possible to perform a dash and gain invincibility frames. This makes the combat significantly easier than in similar games, as the player doesn't have to commit to attacks in the same way as they would in, say, a FromSoftware game, leaving them locked into a position where they can be countered.

Sébastien Benard's action roguelike has resurfaced with a release window after several years of radio silence.

The quick dash is more effective when using Slash Gordon, as it synergizes well with a swift weapon. This isn't to say that the Wolfhammer isn't also broken in its own way, as it has a breath weapon-style attack that can be merged with a Frost Rune to perform multiple hits that each have a chance of inflicting the Freeze status effect on an enemy, drastically increasing the chance of paralyzing them.

This makes the combat significantly easier than in similar games, as the player doesn't have to commit to attacks in the same way as they would in, say, a FromSoftware game, leaving them locked into a position where they can be countered.

Murals is still a work-in-progress, so there’s plenty of time for developers to tweak the gameplay balance. What’s here is considerably easier than many of the action RPGs on the market, but the reason for that could be related to the fact that it’s a mostly linear, story-based game, with few roguelike elements.

The levels in Murals might look like the randomly connected rooms of countless roguelikes, but the stages have been crafted and designed to tell a story, including NPC encounters, puzzles, and even side quests. While there are some random elements, such as how the upgrades/Eeries are handled, the bulk of the game is a planned affair, which explains why it’s easier than its contemporaries.

Each level in Murals is a stunning, hand-drawn piece of artwork, where every room appears lovingly crafted and filled with little touches to admire while exploring

It's a bold move to go for a linear approach in a market so consumed with randomness, especially when Murals uses a gameplay style and overall aesthetic that’s tied to roguelikes. That being said, there’s plenty of room for a more focused and narrative-driven title that uses the gameplay loop of familiar titles, especially when the levels look this good.

Murals has a ton of potential and an amazing pedigree behind it. Dlala Studios has produced some amazing titles in the past, and the fact that the game is so polished and impressive at this point in development is a feat unto itself. The hard part is going to be tweaking the combat to make it satisfying for everyone, meaning some strict difficulty modifiers could be the answer.

The comedic writing and tone in Murals are trickier, as they're so baked into the game’s identity, yet also have the potential to miss the mark. It’s the kind of thing that someone will know they’re going to enjoy within a short period of time, and hopefully, Mural’s subversive take on fairy tales is as appealing to the audience as its combat.

This morning, Nintendo shared some updates related to the Pikmin franchise and has officially claimed November 1 as Pikmin Day, starting today and moving forward presumably forever.

A free demo for the game, which will include one standard level and two Dandori Academy levels, will be available on November 2.

#4271. Gobs & Gears turns factory building into a goblin-powered demolition puzzle

The best advice Gobs & Gears gives you is to build it wrong. It may sound counterintuitive, but you lay out a route, rip it up the moment it’s done its job, and blow up the odd building along the way, all to finish a bomb for a goblin king who wants it immediately. It’s a logistics puzzler that’s out now on iPhone.

The map starts under a thick Fog. Just like London has been the past few days. You put up Scout Towers to burn it back in bursts, and each surge reveals lost Buildings that need to be brought back. For that, you need the right resources, which must be hauled around by Trundlers along conveyor routes you lay yourself. And if a mountain gets in your way, just blow it up.

Crafting runs from Rubble at the bottom to the Boom Core at the top, across sixteen resources, six tiers and 26 kinds of Building. Gobs from nearby Gob Camps can speed a building up or carry resources from places your routes haven’t reached yet. The maps are procedurally generated too, with roughly 281 quadrillion possible layouts.

Factory games like these make you live with your mistakes. A messy layout tends to stay messy. Gobs & Gear makes rebuilding the point. I’d say Mini Motorways is the nearest relative, where half the time you’re pulling up the road you placed five minutes ago.

There’s no grinding between runs and no punishing timers either. Given the Gob King’s mood, I thought there’d be a timer. It’s all pixel art, and the building names do a fair bit of the joking, the Smelty Hole and the Dig Pit among them.

Gobs & Gears is out today on iOS for a one-off $9.99 purchase.

If you’d prefer puzzles with fewer explosions, our list of the best strategy games on iOS is mostly bomb-free.

#4270. Diablo 4's next expansion is bringing two new classes to the game, one of which you can play right now

Lord of Hatred may finally make good on the Mephisto arc of Diablo 4's campaign, which started in the original game and carried through Vessel of Hatred.

Very much when we expected it, Blizzard has officially revealed Diablo 4’s next major expansion at The Game Awards. Lord of Hatred delivers a new campaign that continues the mainline story, picking up from where Vessel of Hatred left off. Mephisto, the eponymous Lord of Hatred, has seemingly finally escaped imprisonment to rule over Sanctuary.

Lord of Hatred is the second Diablo 4 expansion, and it will be available on PC, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on April 28.

It’s always a big deal when we get a new Diablo expansion, especially for a game as starved of fresh (major) content as Diablo 4 has been. But perhaps the biggest piece of news out of the Lord of Hatred reveal is that the expansion is bringing not one, but two new classes to the game.

The first of which is The Paladin, whereas the second is being kept under wraps. Even more surprising is that The Paladin is playable right now for anyone who pre-purchases the expansion. This is a well-timed shadow drop, especially given that Diablo 4’s latest season has just kicked off.

The expansion adds a new region to the world: Skovos, which is where the events of the new campaign will be taking place. This is the first time Skovos has been in a Diablo game. The region is of major significance to the world and lore of the series, as it is the birthplace of the firstborn, home of Lilith and Inaruis.

Lord of Hatred brings a decent number of major systems to Diablo 4. The endgame is getting a big overhaul, headlined by the new War Plans feature. Through this, you can effectively design your own endgame grind, creating challenges based on the activities you like and earning rewards along the way.

Endgame activities now also feature their own skill trees, which can be progressed through by creating War Plans for your character featuring each activity. The new endgame activity, Echoing Hatred, is something of horde mode where you must defend against unrelenting waves of enemies.

None of that matters without loot, of course, and the upcoming expansion is bringing back the Horadric Cube, and adding set bonuses using the Talisman system. The long-awaited and highly-requested Loot Filter is also coming to the game with the release of the expansion.

Beyond itemisation, each class’ skill tree will grow with new bonus skill variants. In fact, the entire skill system is being reworked for all classes - though details are a little sparse at the moment.

You can also expect the level cap to go up, which is very likely necessary to fit all the new skills and various systems. Blizzard offered a deep dive into the new Paladin class, which you see on the official blog.

#4269. Yakuza Creator Toshiro Nagoshi's Studio Has Officially Shut Down, Ending Gang Of Dragon's Development With It

Nagoshi Studio, the developer led by Yakuza/Like a Dragon series creator Toshiro Nagoshi, has officially shut down, ending development of Gang of Dragon, which was revealed at The Game Awards last year. Shareholders resolved to dissolve the studio on October 31, according to a notice published in a Japanese government newspaper called Kanpo, as first reported by Gematsu.

This follows a report from Bloomberg earlier this year that said Chinese gaming megacorp NetEase Games was cutting funding to Nagoshi Studio, allowing Nagoshi to seek independent funding elsewhere. It seems he couldn't find funding, and now Nagoshi Studio is no more. NetEase helped Nagoshi found the studio in November 2021.

This closure follows other signals that NetEase is looking to divest from the gaming scene outside of its Chinese studios. A little over a month ago, Suda51's Grasshopper Manufacture left NetEase to go independent again, just months after the launch of Romeo Is A Dead Man.

By winning both casual players and hardcore consumers over, Take-Two is in the best spot of maybe any individual studio in the industry, able to secure the positions of their successful employees while prepping them for the next big thing, alongside the mountains of new blood they can afford to bring onto the squad.

#4267. The highly-anticipated follow-up to Baldur's Gate 3 is more Divinity, but it's not technically Original Sin 3

Larian has returned to tease a grand vision for its next major project, a new Divinity.

Larian Studios has delivered what was arguably the biggest reveal of The Game Awards 2025 showcase. The Hellstone, the mysterious monolith in the desert that’s been generating a lot of speculation in the lead-up to the show was indeed teasing the studio’s next game.

The Belgian developer is returning to the series it created with Divinity, a non-numbered sequel that’s designed for new and veteran players alike. The announcement was entirely cinematic, setting the tone for what looks to be the next big thing in the space.

Larian calls Divinity its most ambitious title ever, with the studio striving for a level of depth and breadth we’ve not seen before. This is the next project from the Baldur’s Gate 3 team, after all, so there’s understandably immense anticipation for it.

Divinity is a standalone RPG, and does not require you to have played Divinity: Original Sin, or Divinity: Original Sin 2. If you did, however, you’re going to find the journey extra special because of the continuity it offers.

“We’re ready to bring everything we’ve done previously into one place,” said founder and game director, Swen Vincke.

“This marks the beginning of something with more breadth, depth, and intimacy than anything we’ve created before. We’ve been building toward this moment ever since we took our fate into our own hands. This is the Divinity we’ve always wanted to make and you're going to have loads of fun with it.”

Beyond that, there’s precious little that’s been revealed for Divinity so far. We don’t know what platforms it’s going to be coming to, nor do we even have a release target. We do know it’s an RPG, so you can very much expect something similar to earlier games in the series, and, of course, Baldur’s Gate 3.

The latest charts data from the UK is in, and as expected, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has debuted at the top spot, beating out the likes of Modern Warfare 4 and FC 27.

While not surprising, it's nevertheless a satisfying result, and we'd be keen to see what the actual split is between physical copies and digital. We suspect that, with the pre-order bonuses and midnight launches, physical has likely vastly outsold digital in this case.

In fact, Chris Dring from The Game Business has stated that Ocarina of Time is the second biggest UK physical launch in franchise history, beating Breath of the Wild by around 35% but falling short of Tears of the Kingdom by about half. #4264. Arc Raiders' Cold Snap update brings snow storms to most maps, new events and a new Raider Deck

Arc Raiders has delivered a big new update that's very fittingly on theme, and it's not without new mechanics.

Arc Raiders is kicking off its last major event of the year. The Cold Snap update arrives moments from now, and it’s perhaps the game’s biggest since its momentous launch in late October. We’ve known about the existence of Cold Snap for a while, of course, but we finally have a solid idea about what to expect.

Cold Snap is made up of different components - including new content - that all players have access to.

As the name suggests, of course, Cold Snap introduces the new snowfall Map Condition. As part of this, maps will be covered in snow, thanks to snowstorms sweeping across them. For one, snowfall makes it harder to see enemies, but it also turns all lakes solid.

There’s a new mechanic associated with this, and it’s actually similar to Battlefield 6’s Winter Offensive update. Staying outdoors for too long will cause you to catch frostbite, which slowly drains HP. Embark says you’re going to need to bring more healing items with you on raids, and it doesn’t look like there are firepits that could keep you warm - though staying indoors for a while will help.

Cold Snap arrives alongside limited-time events that will be available until Tuesday, January 13. The snowfall visual update and new frostbite mechanics are available on Dam Battlegrounds, Buried City, Spaceport, and The Blue Gate.

One of the new events is Flickering Flames, which comes with its own progression track of 25 levels. Content is, of course, unlocked using Merits, which are earned from XP in matches. The other event is the Candleberry Banquet Project, which requires you to donate items found on the surface (including Candleberries).

You’ll earn rewards each time, and each stage completed will reveal a new scene on the banquet table. Likewise, there are cosmetic rewards as part of each stage, and you can use it as a source of Merits, too.

While on the subject, the new update also kicks off a new Raider Deck (battle pass). Available from December 26, The Goalie Raider Deck is pretty much what you’d expect. You’ll find several pages of cosmetic and useful items. The new Deck will be available to all players for free.

#4262. Angry Birds Dream Blast takes you back to the Angry Birds Movie 2 in new event

With the Angry Birds Movie 3 set to land in cinemas soon, it's no surprise that Rovio are eager to get people back in the silver screen mood. And now Angry Birds Dream Blast is throwing you back to the original sequel, with a new in-game event devoted to the Angry Birds Movie 2.

The event will see you play through content inspired by the Angry Birds Movie 2 and relive the events of the film for yourself. It also sees the introduction of the Dream Album mechanic, which lets you earn even more rewards themed around the film for completing levels. I wouldn't be surprised if part of this is inspired by their acquisition by Sega, as Rovio have also teased a cameo by Sonic the Hedgehog in the new film. All this, and the event itself, indicates they're promoting the film from multiple angles in new and exciting ways.

But for Angry Birds Dream Blast fans, all you need to know is that this event offers a suite of new rewards and content for you to enjoy. And if you need to refresh yourself on a childhood favourite, keep your eyes peeled for the return of the Angry Birds Movie to select theatres on November 13th!

In the meantime, if you want to refresh yourself on some of the other great releases on mobile this year as we speed towards Christmas, why not check out our list of the best mobile games of 2026 (so far) for some choice picks?

#4261. Arc Raiders' latest patch adds two of the most requested features, but kills Cred hoarding

The last major Arc Raiders update of the year has arrived, bringing several big new features to the game, but not without some bad news.

Embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere. This is a significant patch for the extraction shooter for a number of reasons, not least of which because it kicks off a series of events under the Cold Snap banner, which introduces a new conditions to the game’s maps.

Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.

To start with, today’s update finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights. This is especially relevant for PC players, most of whom play shooters with an ADS toggle, rather than hold. Another often requested feature has been the ability to reset the game’s skill tree.

This is now available for the cost of 2,000 Coins per skill point. It goes without saying that you’re going to need a whole lot of money to reset the entire thing, but it’s a useful option to have when you want to alter your path.

The next change is one that’s going to ruffle a lot of feathers. Arc Raiders now has a soft Cred cap of 800. This is now clearly shown on your Wallet screen, and the developer said the cap is necessary to prevent players from using their accumulated Cred to unlock new Raider Decks immediately after release.

The good news is that this won’t affect the Cred you may already have, but going forward, 800 is the most you can hold at any point. You’ll also notice that Shani has more stuff for you to buy with Cred, in case you want another way to spend what you have.

Patch 1.7.0 also brings a few other additions - and makes some changes - that are worth highlighting. You can now customise your Raider Tool, which likely means we’re going to see Raider Tool cosmetics going forward.

Speaking of items, the Aphelion weapon blueprint has been moved to Stella Montis, so you won’t be able to get it from taking down the Matriarch. The Bettina, and Rattler have both seen some balance changes.

The Bettina’s durability will now degrade a lot slower per shot, making it take 26 magazines to fully deplete durability. The base magazine size has been increased to 22, and the reload time has been cut to 4.5 seconds. Embark says this should make the weapon more viable in PvP, while also allowing it to stand on its own without the need for players bring a secondary weapon.

As for the Rattler, the only change it gets is an increase to its magazine size from 10 to 12. The idea is to make it about as effective as a Stitcher or Kettle at close ranges when it comes to PvP encounters.

And, of course, it wouldn’t be a big Arc Raiders patch without some tweaks to the game’s Arc enemies. This time, the Shredder gets all the love. The menacing unit now moves faster, turns more sharply and doesn’t get knocked back as much when shot.

The Shredder’s head now has more health, too, meaning you won’t be able to shoot it off early and confuse it. In general, the Arc unit should be smarter, especially when navigating narrow spaces. Finally, the Shredder now activates faster upon detecting (and being attacked by) players.

Beyond that, the main menu has seen a few changes to highlight ongoing events, make certain announcements quieter, make it easier to track Raider Quests and more. There’s a lot more in this update, too, such as changes to footstep loudness, several tweaks to loot and the value of certain items, and more besides. You’ll find the full change log on the official website.

#4260. It’s official: Battlefield 6 is 2025's best-selling game, but Black Ops 7 still managed to be November’s top-seller

2025 will be remembered for many things, but in the ultra-competitive games industry, it’s going to be thought of as the year Battlefield 6 did what many thought couldn’t happen.

Circan’s November 2025 video game sales report has easily been one of the most anticipated. For one, November is always one of the most lucrative for the games industry, but this year in particular has seen several major hits - including new entries in two rival series.

We’re talking, of course, about Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 the latest releases in their respective multiplayer shooter series. The decades-old fight to claim the top spot has long been won by Call of Duty, but the latest Battlefield has achieved what many thought was impossible.

Cricana’s report covers spending on video game software, hardware, and accessories in the U.S. November 2025 saw spending fall by 4% compared to November 2024, bringing in a total of $5.9 billion.

Software technically saw growth during the month, but declines in hardware, and accessories were mainly responsible for the drop in overall spending. Black Ops 7 continued Call of Duty’s 18-Year Streak in topping sales in its launch month.

However, this year’s game did not also top the year-to-date charts, something the series has done consistently, and more than any other top-selling game each year - with rare exceptions. Battlefield 6 is firmly in the lead there, cementing its claim as 2025’s best-selling title. Black Ops 7, fittingly, occupies in the #7 spot there.

Separately from the best-selling game title fight, November has actually been one of the worst for the industry in terms of hardware sales. The report notes that the three major platform holders - Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo have all seen their hardware sales decline.

Spending on hardware during November amounted to only $695 million, a massive 27% decline compared to November 2024. According to the report, that’s the worst dollar amount total for any November since 2005, when it comes to hardware specifically. All three current-gen consoles totaled 1.6 million units sold, which Circana also notes is the lowest for any November since 1995.

This all doesn’t bode especially well for the industry. November has always been a key holiday shopping month, but it’s clear the constantly rising console prices - and already high game prices - have had a big impact.

#4259. Zenless Zone Zero's big end-of-year update brings multiplayer combat, free Zhao, and the first dual-form Agent

Zenless Zone Zero' is saying goodbye to 2025 with a bang, as update 2.5 gets fully revealed.

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program has delivered the good news on Version 2.5, To Be Fuel for the Night. This chapter is a big deal for a few reasons, not least of which because it brings an end to Season 2.

To start with, Version 2.5 arrives on December 30, making it the game’s last major update of the year, which also means players are in for some freebies to celebrate the new year.

Of course, the biggest addition in Version 2.5 is Ye Shunguang, the game’s new Agent, who’s a Void Hunter, and also Zenless Zone Zero’s first dual-form Agent. Zhao also becomes a playable Agent as part of this update - two things HoYoverse teased last week at The Game Awards.

Ye Shunguang’s unique attribute is Honed Edge, through which she can enter an Enlightened Mind state. Ye Shunguang’s signature Ether Veil can deliver Honed Edge damage as she applies a vulnerability effect to enemies. She arrives alongside her sidekick, Bangboo Sprout, who keeps with her swordplay theme by calling down flying swords.

Zhao is the other playable Agent as mentioned, an S-Rank Ice Defence legend. Zhao is a fast and nimble attacker who uses her giant greataxe to suppress enemies. Zhao can trigger Ether Veil: Wellspring by using Frostbite she accumulates, which buffs the entire squad.

Narratively, this particular chapter will reveal the fate of Waifei Peninsula. The quest is gonna take the squad deeper into the Lumite Mine ruins, and the new Perception Technique is how you’ll uncover the answers hidden within.

There’s a gameplay component to that, too. Ye Shunguang's Bladeflash Mirage ability will come in handy during the story’s big investigation, which comes with unique rewards, including a new W-Engine.

Version 2.5 is also the one set to give players the first taste of multiplayer combat thought he limited-time Joint Investigation: The Divine Maze event. As part of that, you can have three-Agent squads face off against each other in unique combat challenges.

There’s even more to get excited about in this one. Proxy Outpost lets you create your own Outposts, and join those created by other. This is more of a social feature than anything, though.

HoYoverse is also making a series of updates to Soldier 11, Grace, Soldier 0 – Anby, Ellen, and Burnice, all of whom will see their mechanics updated and their effectiveness boosted. Similar updates are on the way for other Agents, which will arrive in future updates. Shiyu Defense and Deadly Assault has seen some adjustments to the gameplay loop, too.

Finally, HoYoverse is making it easier for players to jump into 2.5’s new story chapter using Advance Screening. Ye Shunguang and Zhao will be available for the entire update’s duration, and reruns in the second half will guarantee another S-Rank.

You’ll be able to pick from Alice, Soldier 0 – Anby, or Astra. Zhao will herself be available as a login bonus alongside 1,000 Polychromes, a new outfit for Jane, and more. If you’re looking to jump in on December 30, don’t do so without having a look at our Zenless Zone Zero codes page to get some freebies.

#4257. GTA 6 Will Be Playable on XBOX One, According to Rockstar

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

A big part of what’s making the steadily-encroaching release of Grand Theft Auto 6 interesting in the current gaming climate, besides, y’know, being Grand Theft Auto 6, is that it’s only going to be available on consoles, and specifically XBOX and PlayStation family consoles. PC and Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 are being left out in the cold, at least for the time being, although rumors abound that the PC launch may come sooner than expected in order to beat out AI slop knockoffs.

I don’t claim to know all of the precise reasons for this particular launch strategy, beyond perhaps a pursuit for immediate at-launch optimization for the most readily-available consoles. That said, it would seem that, even if you own a particular console from the previous generation, you may still be able to play the game, albeit in a slightly diminished state.

Rockstar announced on its official news blog today that pre-loading for Grand Theft Auto 6 has officially begun, with the many who pre-ordered the game digitally now able to start downloading, and those who purchased codes-in-boxes able to start redeeming them and do the same. Buried within this announcement was a rather unexpected detail: it’ll be possible to play Grand Theft Auto 6 on the previous generation’s XBOX One console.

GTA 6, Rockstar's upcoming open-world adventure, is taking up 210 GB on PlayStation 5.

Here’s the interesting bit: since XBOX Cloud Gaming is also available on the XBOX One console, that means you can, in fact, play Grand Theft Auto 6 on an XBOX One by streaming it. At least as far as I’ve determined, the XBOX One will be the only previous-gen console that will be able to play this brand-new game, and an exceptionally high-end game at that.

Since XBOX Cloud Gaming is also available on the XBOX One console, that means you can, in fact, play Grand Theft Auto 6 on an XBOX One.

Of course, there are some catches here. First, no matter what XBOX console you’re playing on, any instance of Grand Theft Auto 6 played via Cloud Gaming will use XBOX Series S-tier graphical settings, i.e. not the best possible ones. Additionally, as is always the case with cloud streaming, how good the game looks and runs is largely dependent on the quality of your internet connection, so if you’ve got lousy speeds, this isn’t going to work well for you.

As GTA 6's launch approaches, everyone wants part of the PR pie, including internet ISPs.

On a semi-related note, Rockstar also confirmed that Grand Theft Auto 6 will work with Remote Play on both PlayStation and XBOX consoles, for those who want to stream the game from their console to elsewhere in their home.

I probably don’t need to remind anybody of this, but here it is anyway: Grand Theft Auto 6 is officially launching on Thursday, November 19, with the unlock time being whenever the clock strikes midnight in your particular time zone.

Whether through an installed digital copy or, apparently, on an XBOX One via Cloud Gaming, anyone who is interested in this game will, with certainty, be playing it as soon as it launches. I shudder to think what those poor digital storefronts are going to be going through at midnight on the 19th. Maybe wait until after school or work that day before you try to start playing, at least assuming you’re not one of the metric whoa-ton of people who are projected to be calling in sick that day.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is encroaching upon our reality, and upon its advent, there is a non-zero chance life will never be the same. If you’re not too busy playing the game for an indeterminate blur of time, maybe you can check out Rockstar’s official launch party in Miami the following weekend.

A massive music festival will be held in Miami the weekend following the game's release, with numerous big-name performers to participate.

#4256. FC 26 adds upgraded Pina alongside 3 new Heroes in full Winter Wildcards promo

Winter Wildcards Team 1 is scarier than Ultimate Scream, featuring buffed Pina, Dembele, Valverde and Rodman cards alongside brand-new Heroes.

EA Sports has revealed 3 new Heroes coming to FC 26 Ultimate Team as part of Team 1 of the Winter Wildcards promo: Ivan Zamorano, Claudio Pizarro and Jill Scott.

The Bayern and Werder Bremen legend Claudio Pizarro is famously the Bundesliga’s oldest ever player, after turning out well past 40 years of age - up front no less. But he’s making an appearance in FC 26 because he won the Hero Vote Poll a few months ago, with the Peruvian edging out notable nutter Steffan Effenberg and the prolific Brazilian striker, Elber.

The love for South American Heroes continues with Ivan Zamorano presented in his Real Madrid guise rather than part of the unbelievably stacked Inter squad which featured legends and Icons ranging from current Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone to Javier Zanetti and Ronaldo Nazario.

And probably most interestingly, Queen of the Jungle and centurion Lioness, Jill Scott, is also coming to shore up the midfield with a card which fits the “Gullit Gang” pre-requisite of all face stats over 80 - including a dominant 91 physical befitting her role as one of the most recognisable enforcers in women’s football.

Whether her in-game body type will actually let her put that strength out on the pitch (she will surely also have Bruiser) remains to be seen, but she could easily have the gangly aura of Patrick Vieira if the rest of her PlayStyles are right.

New Ultimate Team Heroes have been added mid-season before, including the likes of Enzo Francescoli in FC 24, but 3 at once looks to indicate that EA is leaning on Heroes to add fan-favourite players to the game with a lower threshold than Icons.

Plus they can be given away for free without upsetting the power curve as much as Icons, as shown by the free Classic XI Heroes handed out recently (I got Mario Gomez, F).

The rest of the Winter Wildcards team features a host of equally famous, and now infamous, players with some featuring 99 stats and alternative positions.

Highlights include striker and CAM versions of Balon D’or holder Ousmane Dembele, but also everyone’s love-to-hate Low Driven Shot master, Claudia Pina.

There are also incredibly strong-looking Gabriel and Fede Valverde cards, as well as downgraded, and therefore hopefully cheaper, versions of Icons like Johan Cruyff.

#4255. The Elder Scrolls VI Has An Official Subtitle And It's 'Sentinel'

The headline tells the story: The Elder Scrolls VI has an official subtitle and it's Sentinel. So the full game is now titled The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel, or, as we will undoubtedly refer to it moving forward, as we colloquially do with the previous three games (Morrowind, Oblivion, and Skyrim), Sentinel.

The news comes from Bethesda's various social media accounts, which are all sharing the video above. Along with the video, music, and the title, it also shares the text as a quote attributed to Yazar, Moth Priest to High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell (4E 206): "The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate."

Sentinel is one of the nine major kingdoms within Hammerfell and is the capital of both the Alik'r Desert region and the Myrkwasa region of the Alik'r (source: elderscrolls.fandom). With this knowledge, it's fair to assume Sentinel will have many desert locations.

The name continues the tradition of naming the games after locations in the Elder Scrolls universe. Oblivion is the sort of exception, as it is a realm, but it still counts. We still don't know exactly when The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel will be released, but we're now about seven years from its original announcement at E3 2018.

#4253. Big Walk Ineligible For IGF Game Of The Year Due To AI Use

AI use in video games has never been a more hotly debated topic, and much like last year with Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, its masked use during development has impacted one of this year’s Game of the Year frontrunners, Big Walk. Turns out AI was used during Big Walk’s development, and it’s the game’s disqualification from the Independent Game Festival’s GOTY consideration that has led to that unfortunate discovery.

The IGF posted a statement (thanks, Aftermath) regarding its nominations this year, highlighting that some who vote for its GOTY nominees and award winners simply won’t consider games that used generative AI during their development. It seemed a fairly straightforward, somewhat expected stance. However, it became clear in the hours after that statement was posted that the reason IGF representatives were having such a tough time deliberating is because AI was used during Big Walk’s development.

As the BDS Boycott continues, Big Walk stands firm.

That revelation has led to Big Walk studio House House updating its FAQ to confirm that yes, AI was used during the game’s development process, and to explain how exactly it was implemented.

“In the final stretch of Big Walk’s development, LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs,” the new FAQ section reads.

LLM stands for large language model, AIs that are trained on vast amounts of text to help summarize, translate, and in some cases generate language.

“In some cases, snippets from LLM responses were copied as a starting point to be modified into game code - we’d estimate that well under 0.1% of Big Walk’s code had anything to do with this usage, and generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game.”

The updated FAQ section continues, providing examples of when House House turned to AI during the latter stages of Big Walk’s development for help. It goes on to explain that a version of this was sent to IGF to clarify the studio’s use of AI, hence it being seemingly disqualified from GOTY consideration, and the matter becoming public knowledge.

House House then adds that the reason it didn’t disclose the use of AI during Big Walk’s development until now is because it isn’t mandatory on Steam, and that it is only disclosing the information now because “it’s a matter of public interest”. Letting your players know AI was used during development is arguably always a matter of public interest, not just when you get found out for not disclosing it in the first place, but it’s the arguably in that sentence that makes AI use in video games so divisive.

In the explanation’s penultimate paragraph, House House writes, "We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as 'inevitable'." Again, it might be argued that other studios see this and think quite the opposite, seeing Big Walk’s huge success and turning to AI also, and hiding it, since it worked for House House.

Big Walk will now not be considered for IGF’s GOTY award, and this could result in a knock-on effect where it fails to pick up nominations elsewhere. It has already been nominated for the Golden Joysticks GOTY, the winner of which will be announced this week. Even after winning, though, Big Walk might not be safe from having its win revoked. Expedition 33 lost its Indie Game Awards GOTY last year after AI use during development was unearthed after the GOTY had been awarded. The award was retroactively taken back and given to runner-up Blue Prince instead.

"I think most of the confusion boils down to context."
